title: 633. Joan of Arc: Saviour of France (Part 2)

sentences.en: King of England, and you, Duke of Bedford, who call yourself Regent of the Kingdom of France, you, William Paul, Count of Suffolk, John Tolbott, and you, Thomas Lord Scales,
sentences.zh: 英格兰国王，还有你，自称法兰西王国摄政的贝德福德公爵，你，萨福克伯爵威廉·保尔，约翰·托尔博特，还有你，斯卡尔斯勋爵托马斯，

sentences.en: who call yourselves Lieutenants of the said Duke of Bedford, make satisfaction to the King of Heaven.
sentences.zh: 你们这些自称贝德福德公爵副手的人，向天上的国王谢罪吧。

sentences.en: Surrender to the maid who is sent here by God, the King of Heaven, the keys of all the good towns which you have taken and violated in France.
sentences.zh: 把你们在法兰西攻占和蹂躏的所有好城池的钥匙，交还给这位由上帝——天上的国王派来的圣女。

sentences.en: She has come here by God's will to reclaim the kingdom for its rightful King.
sentences.zh: 她遵照上帝的旨意来到这里，为合法的国王收复王国。

sentences.en: She is perfectly ready to make peace if you are willing to grant her satisfaction by abandoning France and paying for what you have held.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意撤出法兰西并赔偿你所占领的一切来向她谢罪，她完全准备好缔结和平。

sentences.en: And you, archers, men at war, gentlemen and others, who are before the town of Orléans, get going back to your own country in the name of God.
sentences.zh: 而你们，在奥尔良城前的弓箭手、战士、绅士及其他人，奉上帝之名回你们自己的国家去吧。

sentences.en: And should you not do so, then expect tidings from the maid, who will come to see you shortly to your very great arm.
sentences.zh: 若你们不这样做，那就等着圣女的消息吧，她很快就会来找你们，给你们带来极大的祸患。

sentences.en: King of England, if you do not do so, I am a captain of war, and in whatever place I meet your people in France, I shall compel them to depart, whether they want to or not.
sentences.zh: 英格兰国王，如果你不这样做，我乃是一名战将，无论我在法兰西何处遇到你的人，我都将强迫他们离开，不管他们愿不愿意。

sentences.en: And if they refuse to obey, then I will have them all put to death.
sentences.zh: 如果他们拒绝服从，我便将他们全部处死。

sentences.en: I am sent here by God, the King of Heaven, to drive you out of France.
sentences.zh: 我奉天上的国王上帝之命来到这里，旨在将你们赶出法兰西。

sentences.en: So that's one of the most remarkable letters in history.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是历史上最了不起的信件之一。

sentences.en: And it was dictated, not written, dictated, on the 22nd of March, 1429, by an illiterate peasant girl to the King of England and his captains who were in France.
sentences.zh: 它是由一个不识字的农村女孩在1429年3月22日口述的——注意是口述，而非亲笔书写——写给当时在法兰西的英格兰国王及其将领们的。

sentences.en: And these captains, since the previous October, 1428,
sentences.zh: 而这些将领们，自前一年也就是1428年10月以来，

sentences.en: had been laying siege to the city of Orléans on the River Loire, the lynchpin of the front line between the English and Dauphin-held possessions in France.
sentences.zh: 一直在对卢瓦尔河畔的奥尔良城实施围攻，该城是英格兰势力与法兰西太子势力之间前线的核心支柱。

sentences.en: Now, by the spring of 1429, the city of Orléans seemed about to fall.
sentences.zh: 到了1429年春，奥尔良城似乎就要失守了。

sentences.en: And if it did fall, then the English would be able to drive a stake into the heart of their enemy's holdings,
sentences.zh: 如果它真的失守，那么英格兰人就能在敌方领地的核心楔入一颗钉子，

sentences.en: and possibly bring an end at last to the noble crusade of the Hundred Years' War.
sentences.zh: 并最终可能为这场高尚的百年十字军东征画上句号。

sentences.en: But this peasant girl, Tom, had other ideas.
sentences.zh: 但汤姆，这个农村女孩却有别的想法。

sentences.en: Now, who on earth is she?
sentences.zh: 话说回来，她到底是何方神圣？

sentences.en: Who are we talking about?
sentences.zh: 我们在说谁？

sentences.en: Well, she is, of course, it will stun our listeners to learn,
sentences.zh: 好吧，她当然是——这会让我们的听众大吃一惊——

sentences.en: Joan of Arc, or as she called herself, Jeanne Lapucelle, the maid.
sentences.zh: 圣女贞德，或者按她自己的称呼，贞娜·拉皮塞尔（Jeanne Lapucelle），即圣女。

sentences.en: And in our previous episode, we described her background.
sentences.zh: 在上一期节目中，我们介绍了她的背景。

sentences.en: We described her childhood.
sentences.zh: 我们描述了她的童年。

sentences.en: She'd been born in a village called Domremy on the war-torn eastern margins of France.
sentences.zh: 她出生在法兰西饱受战争蹂躏的东部边缘一个叫栋雷米的小村庄里。

sentences.en: She's a peasant girl.
sentences.zh: 她是个村姑。

sentences.en: And so, by definition, she hasn't learned to ride a horse.
sentences.zh: 因此，从某种意义上说，她从未学过骑马。

sentences.en: She's not practiced in the handling of arMs.
sentences.zh: 她不擅长使用武器。

sentences.en: But then, at the age of 13, she hears a voice that she says has come from heaven.
sentences.zh: 但在她13岁时，她听到了一种声音，她称这声音来自天堂。

sentences.en: And these are soon to become voices in the plural.
sentences.zh: 这些声音很快就变成复数了。

sentences.en: And by 1428, these voices are telling her to lead an army to Orleans and to break the English siege.
sentences.zh: 到了1428年，这些声音指示她带领军队去奥尔良打破英格兰人的围城。

sentences.en: And so, she obeys.
sentences.zh: 于是，她服从了。

sentences.en: And she sets out on this mission in February 1429.
sentences.zh: 她在1429年2月踏上了这项使命。

sentences.en: She has a horse.
sentences.zh: 她有一匹马。

sentences.en: She's riding it.
sentences.zh: 她正骑着它。

sentences.en: And she sets off on what is a very long and dangerous journey through territory infested by bandits and men-at-arms, partisans of the hostile Duke of Burgundy.
sentences.zh: 她踏上了一段漫长而危险的旅程，穿越布满土匪和武装人员、敌对勃艮第公爵党羽出没的领地。

sentences.en: And it's an astonishing mission.
sentences.zh: 这是一项令人震惊的使命。

sentences.en: And the one thing we've not done is to describe Joan, to make her come alive for our listeners.
sentences.zh: 我们唯一还没做的事就是描述贞德的模样，让她在听众脑海中鲜活起来。

sentences.en: So, give us a sense of what you'd have seen if you looked up from your job, as you would undoubtedly have been doing, Tom.
sentences.zh: 那么，给我们讲讲，如果你从工作抬起头来——毫无疑问你当时正在劳作，汤姆——你会看到什么样的人。

sentences.en: You'd have been tilling the fields had you lived in the Middle Ages because you're a man of the soil, horny-handed son of toil.
sentences.zh: 如果你生活在中世纪，你一定在田里耕作，因为你是个泥腿子，饱经风霜的劳动之子。

sentences.en: You're not cut out for life as a cleric.
sentences.zh: 你天生不是当神职人员的料。

sentences.en: So, you'd have been working probably near the bottom of the social spectrum.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可能在社会的最底层劳作。

sentences.en: And you'd have looked up and you'd have seen this person passing.
sentences.zh: 当你抬起头，你会看到这个人路过。

sentences.en: What would you have seen?
sentences.zh: 你会看到什么？

sentences.en: The descriptions of Joan are kind of scanty and not entirely reliable.
sentences.zh: 关于贞德的记载相当稀少，且并非完全可靠。

sentences.en: But she seems to have been dark-haired and she has cut this hair, cropped it short in the style of a knight.
sentences.zh: 但她似乎有着黑发，而且把头发剪短了，剪成骑士那种短发。

sentences.en: Someone who knew her well, her future squire, described her as being beautiful and well-formed.
sentences.zh: 一个非常了解她的人，她未来的随从，形容她美丽且身材匀称。

sentences.en: And she does seem to have been attractive.
sentences.zh: 她似乎确实很有吸引力。

sentences.en: But she is not dressed as a woman.
sentences.zh: 但她没有穿女装。

sentences.en: She is dressed as a man.
sentences.zh: 她穿着男装。

sentences.en: And specifically, she is wearing hoes.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，她穿着紧身裤。

sentences.en: She's wearing britches and these are both tightly knotted into a kind of a grey doublet.
sentences.zh: 她穿着马裤，这两者都紧紧系在一件灰色的紧身上衣上。

sentences.en: And this is obviously to guard herself against sexual assault.
sentences.zh: 这显然是为了防范性侵犯。

sentences.en: And over this doublet, she wears a black tunic and she has a black cloak.
sentences.zh: 在这件紧身衣外面，她穿着一件黑色短袍，还披着一件黑色斗篷。

sentences.en: She also has a hat.
sentences.zh: 她还戴着一顶帽子。

sentences.en: It's made of wool.
sentences.zh: 它是羊毛做的。

sentences.en: Again, it's black.
sentences.zh: 同样是黑色的。

sentences.en: And she's pulled this over her hair.
sentences.zh: 她把帽子拉下来盖住头发。

sentences.en: As we said, she's riding a horse, even though she had never ridden one before.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，她骑着马，尽管她以前从未骑过。

sentences.en: And it seems that over the course of this journey, she becomes actually a very good horsewoman.
sentences.zh: 似乎在这次旅程中，她实际上成了一名非常出色的骑手。

sentences.en: She's got a sword by her side, the marker of a knight.
sentences.zh: 她身侧佩戴着一把剑，这是骑士的标志。

sentences.en: And in her train, she has two pages and four men at arMs.
sentences.zh: 在她的随从队伍中，有两个侍童和四个武装人员。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a long, long journey.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一段非常漫长的旅程。

sentences.en: 250 miles.
sentences.zh: 足足250英里。

sentences.en: And they ride mostly by night, presumably to avoid detection and to avoid bandits and Burgundians.
sentences.zh: 他们大部分时间在夜间骑行，想必是为了避开搜捕、土匪以及勃艮第人。

sentences.en: And they cross the Loire and it takes them 10 days.
sentences.zh: 他们穿过卢瓦尔河，花了10天时间。

sentences.en: And then finally, they reach a shrine, Sainte-Catharine de Fierbois.
sentences.zh: 最后，他们到达了一个圣地，菲尔布瓦的圣凯瑟琳圣地。

sentences.en: And what's the point of this shrine?
sentences.zh: 这个圣地的意义何在？

sentences.en: Why this shrine in particular?
sentences.zh: 为什么偏偏是这个圣地？

sentences.en: Well, it's sacred to Sainte-Catherine, who we know from later records is very important to Joan.
sentences.zh: 好吧，它是献给圣凯瑟琳的，从后来的记录中我们知道圣凯瑟琳对贞德非常重要。

sentences.en: But Sainte-Catherine at Fierbois is also very important to prisoners of war who have escaped from the English.
sentences.zh: 但菲尔布瓦的圣凯瑟琳对于从英格兰人手中逃脱的战俘来说也极其重要。

sentences.en: They see the Sainte-Catherine in this shrine as their particular patron.
sentences.zh: 他们将这座圣地里的圣凯瑟琳视为他们特有的守护神。

sentences.en: And so there are all kinds of fetters that they've hung up to mark their liberation.
sentences.zh: 因此，这里挂满了各种各样的镣铐，用来纪念他们重获自由。

sentences.en: And so it's a very Joan place to make a halt.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常符合贞德风格的落脚点。

sentences.en: And at this shrine, she dictates a letter to the man who she has come to see, the man that she acknowledges as being the rightful king of France.
sentences.zh: 在这个圣地里，她口述了一封信，写给她前来拜访的那个人，也就是她所承认的法兰西合法国王。

sentences.en: And this is Charles of Valois.
sentences.zh: 这个人就是瓦卢瓦的查理。

sentences.en: So he is the son of the previous king, Charles VI.
sentences.zh: 他是前任国王查理六世的儿子。

sentences.en: He is the heir to the ancestral dynasty that has been sitting on the throne of France and which has been replaced by the House of Lancaster, the English dynasty.
sentences.zh: 他是祖传王朝的继承人，这个王朝曾坐在法兰西的王位上，却被英格兰王朝兰开斯特家族所取代。

sentences.en: And he's not Charles VII yet.
sentences.zh: 而且他现在还不是查理七世。

sentences.en: I mean, he should be Charles VII, but everyone calls him the Dauphin because they think the English have the upper hand and that he's basically doomed to fail, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他本该是查理七世，但每个人都叫他太子，因为他们认为英格兰人占了上风，他基本上注定要失败，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, legally, if you're a supporter of Charles, he is Charles VII.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是说，从法理上讲，如果你支持查理，他就是查理七世。

sentences.en: But he is widely called the Dauphin, I think, for a number of reasons.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，人们普遍叫他太子，有几个原因。

sentences.en: He doesn't have a kingly heir.
sentences.zh: 他没有王位继承人。

sentences.en: He's physically unprepossessing.
sentences.zh: 他的外表毫无王者之气。

sentences.en: People who've seen the first series of Blackadder, he looks a bit like that.
sentences.zh: 看过《黑爵士》第一季的人会觉得他长得有点像那样。

sentences.en: More germanely, he lives under the shadow of a terrible crime, notorious crime, which is the murder at a peace summit back in 1419 of John the Fearless,
sentences.zh: 更贴切地说，他生活在一场可怕罪行的阴影下，那是一桩臭名昭著的罪行，也就是早在1419年的一次和平峰会上，谋杀了

sentences.en: the Duke of Burgundy, who had been the most powerful nobleman in France.
sentences.zh: 无畏约翰，也就是勃艮第公爵，他曾是法兰西最有权势的贵族。

sentences.en: He's got holdings that are not just in the east of France, but in the low countries as well.
sentences.zh: 他的领地不仅在法兰西东部，也在低地国家。

sentences.en: And it was this murder that had driven the son of John the Fearless, Philip, who supricates the good, to enter his alliance with the English.
sentences.zh: 正是这起谋杀案促使无畏约翰的儿子——善者腓力，与英格兰人结盟。

sentences.en: And as you said, the Loire is the marker between these kind of two rival zones of influence.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，卢瓦尔河是这两个敌对势力范围之间的分界线。

sentences.en: South, the Dauphin, Charles VII, as he legally is, that's where he essentially still can draw on support.
sentences.zh: 南部是太子，按法理上的查理七世，那是他基本上仍然可以获得支持的地方。

sentences.en: But north of the Loire, northern France is effectively now an Anglo-Burgundian condominium.
sentences.zh: 但在卢瓦尔河以北，法兰西北部现在实际上是一个英格兰与勃艮第的共管国。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So one other important point about the Dauphin, though, the Dauphin hasn't been crowned, has he?
sentences.zh: 关于太子还有一点很重要，那就是太子还没有加冕，对吧？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So tradition holds that French kings should be crowned in the cathedral in ReiMs.
sentences.zh: 因此，传统认为法兰西国王应该在兰斯的座堂加冕。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But France is in English territory, and until he can get to France and be crowned, people will not accept him as the rightful king of France.
sentences.zh: 但兰斯在英格兰领土内，在她能去兰斯并加冕之前，人们不会承认他是法兰西的合法国王。

sentences.en: That's about right, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 差不多是这样，对吧？

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this is a big problem to which Joan has a solution.
sentences.zh: 这是一个大问题，而贞德有解决的办法。

sentences.en: And she wants to meet the Dauphin so that she can present this solution to him.
sentences.zh: 她想见太子，以便将这个解决方案呈献给他。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And Charles, at this point, is in a great castle called Chinon, which is south of the Loire, not far.
sentences.zh: 此时查理正身处一座名为希农的宏伟城堡中，它位于卢瓦尔河以南，距离不远。

sentences.en: It's about 20 miles from Fierbois, where the Shrine of St. Catherine is.
sentences.zh: 它距离圣凯瑟琳圣地所在的菲尔布瓦大约20英里。

sentences.en: And when he receives the letter from this illiterate peasant girl, he says, OK, fine, I will meet you.
sentences.zh: 当他收到这个不识字的农村女孩的信时，他说，好吧，行，我会见你。

sentences.en: Despite the fact that plenty of his advisors are advising against it, saying, you know, what if she's a crank?
sentences.zh: 尽管他的许多谋士都劝阻他，说，你知道的，万一她是个怪人呢？

sentences.en: What if she's a fraud?
sentences.zh: 万一她是个骗子呢？

sentences.en: You know, what if she's worse?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，万一更糟呢？

sentences.en: What if she's a sorceress?
sentences.zh: 万一她是女巫呢？

sentences.en: Because the news has come that this girl is dressed as a man, and this is strictly against biblical injunctions.
sentences.zh: 因为有消息传来说这个女孩穿着男装，这严格违背了圣经的诫命。

sentences.en: So, you know, to people who are worried about the possibility that Joan might be a sorceress, the fact that she's wearing male clothing is a kind of warning sign.
sentences.zh: 所以，对于那些担心贞德可能是女巫的人来说，她穿男装这一事实是一个某种程度上的警告信号。

sentences.en: But Charles overrules this advice and agrees that, yeah, I will see this extraordinary person.
sentences.zh: 但查理否决了这些建议，同意说，好吧，我会见见这个非凡的人。

sentences.en: And part of this, presumably, is because he's really up against it.
sentences.zh: 我想，部分原因是他确实已经走投无路了。

sentences.en: He has nothing to lose.
sentences.zh: 他已经没有什么可失去的了。

sentences.en: If Orlean falls, this is a disaster for him.
sentences.zh: 如果奥尔良陷落，对他来说将是一场灾难。

sentences.en: The English will pour across the River Loire into the south.
sentences.zh: 英格兰人将跨过卢瓦尔河涌入南方。

sentences.en: So there's that element to it.
sentences.zh: 所以有这方面的因素。

sentences.en: But also, am I not right in thinking that there are people at his court, not least his mother-in-law,
sentences.zh: 但我也没记错吧，他的朝廷里有人，尤其是他的岳母——

sentences.en: who we talked about last time, who's called Yolande, who is a very impressive woman, who are very keen on Joan, who think that Joan might actually be sent from God?
sentences.zh: 也就是我们上次谈到的名叫约兰德的那位令人印象深刻的女性，他们非常支持贞德，认为贞德可能真的是上帝派来的？

sentences.en: Yeah, so Yolande is, she's the Dowager Duchess of Anjou, and her son, René of Anjou, had his power base in the very region from which Joan is coming.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以约兰德是安茹的太妃公爵夫人，她的儿子安茹的勒内，其权力基础就在贞德来的那个地区。

sentences.en: And so I think it's easy to see, we talked about it in the previous episode, how between them, they might have evaluated Joan and decided that she was worth taking a punt on.
sentences.zh: 所以我想很容易理解——我们在上一集里讨论过——他们之间是如何评估贞德并决定值得在她身上赌一把的。

sentences.en: But why would they have thought that her mission might in any way be plausible?
sentences.zh: 但为什么他们会认为她的使命在任何方面都是合理的呢？

sentences.en: And I think there is an explanation for this, and it's to do with the fact that for decades, even before the arrival of Henry V in France to resume the Hundred Years' War,
sentences.zh: 我认为这有一个解释，它与这样一个事实有关：几十年来，甚至早在亨利五世来到法兰西重燃百年战争之前，

sentences.en: there had been a swirl of prophecies in France foretelling that the kingdom would be redeemed by a virgin sent by God.
sentences.zh: 法兰西就一直流传着各种预言，预言这个王国将由上帝派遣的一位处女所拯救。

sentences.en: So back in the dying days of the 14th century, there had been this visionary Marie d'Avignon who had foretold that an armed maid would emerge to save France in her hour of need.
sentences.zh: 早在14世纪末的最后日子里，就有一位有先知能力的玛丽·达维永，她曾预言一位身披武装的圣女将会在法兰西危急关头崛起以拯救法兰西。

sentences.en: And there were other prophecies too, and these were cited by Christine de Pizan, who we mentioned in the previous episode, this poet who wrote this great eulogy to Joan.
sentences.zh: 还有其他的预言，这些预言被我们在上一集提到过的克里斯蒂娜·德·皮桑引用过，这位女诗人曾为贞德写过一篇伟大的颂词。

sentences.en: And in that poem, Christine listed some of the prophecies.
sentences.zh: 在那首诗中，克里斯蒂娜列举了一些预言。

sentences.en: So to quote her, over 500 years ago, her coming was foreseen by Merlin, the Sybil, and Bede.
sentences.zh: 引用她的话说，500多年前，梅林、西比尔和比德就预见了她的到来。

sentences.en: They wrote of her as someone who would put an end to France's troubles, prophesied she would carry a banner in the French wars, and described all she would achieve.
sentences.zh: 他们在书里将她描绘成一个能结束法兰西麻烦的人，预言她将在法兰西的战争中举起旗帜，并描述了她所要取得的一切成就。

sentences.en: So that too, I think, is part of the context.
sentences.zh: 所以我想这也是背景的一部分。

sentences.en: But I think above all, ultimately what enables Joan to secure her meeting with the Dauphin is her own energy, her own charisma.
sentences.zh: 但我认为最重要的是，最终使贞德能够确保与太子会面的，是她自己的能量和个人魅力。

sentences.en: So she has what Marina Warner in her wonderful book on Joan of Art sums up as an astonishing ability to compel credence.
sentences.zh: 正如玛丽娜·华纳在她关于贞德的精彩著作中所总结的那样，她拥有令人惊叹的强迫他人信服的能力。

sentences.en: But somehow, Joan has a genius for making people believe the most extraordinary things.
sentences.zh: 但不知何故，贞德有一种让人相信最不可思议的事情的天赋。

sentences.en: And it had won over her feudal overlords, say René of Anjou, and the Duke of Lorraine as well.
sentences.zh: 这赢得了她封建领主的信任，比如安茹的勒内，还有洛林公爵。

sentences.en: It had won over Yolande, who's a very kind of hard-boiled, sensible woman.
sentences.zh: 它赢得了约兰德的信任，那是一个相当精明、通情达理的女人。

sentences.en: And in due course, when she comes to meet the Dauphin, it wins over the Dauphin as well.
sentences.zh: 随后来到她与太子见面时，这也赢得了太子的信任。

sentences.en: So they meet in the great hall, the audience chamber at Chinon.
sentences.zh: 于是他们在希农的大厅、接见室里见面了。

sentences.en: And the Dauphin kicks off, doesn't he, by asking Joan her name.
sentences.zh: 太子首先开口问了贞德的名字，对吧？

sentences.en: And she says, I'm called Jeanne Lapucelle.
sentences.zh: 她说，我叫贞娜·拉皮塞尔。

sentences.en: And then comes the great bombshell.
sentences.zh: 接着就是那个重磅炸弹。

sentences.en: Yeah, so Joan goes on, the king of heaven has commanded that through me you are to be consecrated and crowned in the city of ReiMs.
sentences.zh: 是的，接着贞德说，天上的国王命令，通过我，你要在兰斯城接受涂油加冕。

sentences.en: On behalf of our Lord God, I tell you that you are the true heir of France.
sentences.zh: 我奉我们主上帝之名告诉你，你才是法兰西真正的合法继承人。

sentences.en: And then again, she gives the Dauphin her promise, not just that she's going to save Orléans, but that she is going to secure for him the consecration that he desperately craves,
sentences.zh: 然后她再次向太子做出承诺，不仅要拯救奥尔良，而且要为他赢得他极度渴望的加冕，

sentences.en: that he desperately needs if he is going to be accepted by the mass of French people as the legitimate king.
sentences.zh: 如果他想被广大法兰西人民接受为合法国王，他就极其需要这个。

sentences.en: And so she says to him again, God has sent me to take you to ReiMs.
sentences.zh: 所以她再次对他说，上帝派我来带你去兰斯。

sentences.en: Well, this doesn't seem terribly difficult to explain.
sentences.zh: 这似乎并不是很难解释。

sentences.en: I mean, she's basically just telling him what he wants to hear.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她基本上只是在告诉他想听的话。

sentences.en: And in an age when people are interested in prophecies and saints and stuff like that, to have this girl who seems a bit weird turning up and saying, I'm sent by God,
sentences.zh: 在一个人们对预言、圣人和诸如此类的事物感兴趣的时代，突然出现这样一个看起来有点古怪的女孩说，我是上帝派来的，

sentences.en: and I know everything's going to work out all right.
sentences.zh: 而且我知道一切都会好起来的。

sentences.en: I mean, of course he's going to love that, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他当然会喜欢这样，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, he is.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他是会的。

sentences.en: But I mean, again, he's not stupid either.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，话说回来，他也不是个笨蛋。

sentences.en: He's a very smart guy.
sentences.zh: 他是个非常聪明的人。

sentences.en: He needs to be on his guard.
sentences.zh: 他必须保持警惕。

sentences.en: She's come from the region where the Burgundians are very rife.
sentences.zh: 她来自勃艮 Burgundian 人极其猖獗的地区。

sentences.en: What if she has been sent as a Burgundian agent?
sentences.zh: 万一她是被派来的勃艮第间谍呢？

sentences.en: So the fact that he is kind of prepared to take a punt on her, I think is tribute to certainly Joan's powers of persuasion.
sentences.zh: 因此，他愿意冒险相信她，我认为这绝对要归功于贞德的游说能力。

sentences.en: And it's not just the Dauphin who is persuaded.
sentences.zh: 而且不只是王储被说服了。

sentences.en: There is also another guy who is massively smitten by Joan.
sentences.zh: 还有另一个人对贞德迷恋得不得了。

sentences.en: And this is a guy who also is desperate to believe that God might be sending a virgin saviour to redeem France.
sentences.zh: 这个人也迫切地希望相信上帝可能会派遣一位处女救世主来拯救法国。

sentences.en: And this is, again, a guy we met in the previous episode, and he is the Duke of Alençon, Jean.
sentences.zh: 而且，这个人我们也在上一集里见过，他就是阿朗松公爵让。

sentences.en: And by now, this guy is 20.
sentences.zh: 到这个时候，这家伙已经20岁了。

sentences.en: So his father had died at Agincourt.
sentences.zh: 所以他的父亲在阿赞库尔战役中丧生了。

sentences.en: He'd been captured in 1424.
sentences.zh: 他在1424年被俘。

sentences.en: The Duke of Bedford, the English regent, had appropriated all his lands.
sentences.zh: 英格兰摄政王贝德福德公爵侵占了他所有的土地。

sentences.en: The Duke of Alençon had had to kind of mortgage everything to raise his ransom.
sentences.zh: 阿朗松公爵不得不典当一切来筹集赎金。

sentences.en: So basically, he's completely skint.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，他彻底破产了。

sentences.en: And he is known at the court as the poorest man in France, even though he is a Duke of the realm.
sentences.zh: 他在宫廷里被称为法国最穷的人，尽管他是一位王国公爵。

sentences.en: So you can see, again, why Alençon would be desperate to believe in Joan.
sentences.zh: 所以你也能明白，为什么阿朗松会极度渴望相信贞德。

sentences.en: And in fact, he starts taking his meals with her.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他开始和她一起用餐。

sentences.en: He joins her meetings with the Dauphin.
sentences.zh: 他加入了她与王储的会面。

sentences.en: They become great pals.
sentences.zh: 他们成了好哥们。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And he, too, he can sense this sort of conviction in her, this intensity.
sentences.zh: 而且他也能感受到她身上那种坚定的信念，那种强烈的气场。

sentences.en: It's this intensity, actually, that will make her a military leader, right, that she will carry into battle.
sentences.zh: 事实上，正是这种强烈的气场让她成为了一个军事领袖，对吧，她将把这种气场带入战场。

sentences.en: And I think that's a reason why Alençon and perhaps the Dauphin also believe in her, is that they sense that this sense of conviction is something that will inspire their men.
sentences.zh: 我想这也是阿朗松、或许还有王储相信她的原因，因为他们感觉到这种坚定的信念能够鼓舞他们的部下。

sentences.en: And the French armies at this point are demoralized.
sentences.zh: 而此时的法军已经士气低落。

sentences.en: They have zero morale.
sentences.zh: 他们毫无士气可言。

sentences.en: So perhaps this girl with her absolute sense of conviction, perhaps that's just what they need.
sentences.zh: 所以也许这个带着绝对坚定信念的女孩，正是他们所需要的。

sentences.en: And the fact that she is a girl, I mean, as we said in the last episode,
sentences.zh: 而且她是个女孩这一事实，我的意思是，就像我们在上一集里说的，

sentences.en: we did a previous episode about Catherine of Siena, this sort of mystical figure who claimed to have married ChriSt.
sentences.zh: 我们之前做过一期关于锡耶纳的凯瑟琳的节目，这是一个声称自己嫁给了基督的神秘人物。

sentences.en: The fact that she's a woman, you know, that doesn't make her implausible as a messenger from God.
sentences.zh: 她是个女性，你知道的，这并没有让她作为上帝使者的可信度降低。

sentences.en: In fact, it enhances it, right?
sentences.zh: 事实上，这反而增强了可信度，对吧？

sentences.en: Because women have a special place in the, you know, a unique place in the medieval Christian sense of the world.
sentences.zh: 因为女性在中世纪基督教的世界观中占据着特殊的位置，你知道的，一个独一无二的位置。

sentences.en: Women obviously can't be priests, but there is a sense that perhaps that gives them a kind of a more intimate relationship with God.
sentences.zh: 女性显然不能成为神职人员，但人们有一种感觉，也许这赋予了她们与上帝更亲密的关系。

sentences.en: That God can, will sometimes bypass the structure of the church and speak directly to women in a way that he tends not to do to men.
sentences.zh: 上帝可以、有时会绕过教会的体制，以一种他通常对男性不会采用的方式，直接与女性对话。

sentences.en: And Joan, as you said,
sentences.zh: 而贞德，就像你说的，

sentences.en: is absolutely not the first female visionary to be granted interviews with the powerful and the mighty on the basis of their claim that they have been spoken to by the saints and by God.
sentences.zh: 绝不是第一个以圣徒和上帝曾对她们说话为由，得以与权贵和显赫人物面谈的女性先知。

sentences.en: So Catherine of Siena is exactly such a woman because she had ended up a counselor and advisor to popes.
sentences.zh: 所以锡耶纳的凯瑟琳正是这样一位女性，因为她最终成为了教皇的谋士和顾问。

sentences.en: It was Catherine of Siena who had persuaded the Pope in Avignon to move back to Rome.
sentences.zh: 正是锡耶纳的凯瑟琳说服了阿维尼翁的教皇迁回罗马。

sentences.en: So it is possible for women who claim a kind of direct access to God to play a striking role in the affairs of Christendom.
sentences.zh: 因此，声称能够直接接触上帝的女性，完全有可能在基督教世界的事务中发挥惊人的作用。

sentences.en: But against that, to repeat, there is an enormous risk in relying on such people.
sentences.zh: 但话又说回来，重申一遍，依赖这样的人存在着巨大的风险。

sentences.en: Because what if Joan is a fraud?
sentences.zh: 因为万一贞德是个骗子呢？

sentences.en: What if she's been set up by the Burgundians?
sentences.zh: 万一她是勃艮第人设下的局呢？

sentences.en: What if she's delusional?
sentences.zh: 万一她有妄想症呢？

sentences.en: And even if her voices are real, you know, what if they are not from God?
sentences.zh: 退一步讲，就算她听到的声音是真的，你知道的，万一它们不是来自上帝呢？

sentences.en: What if they are from hell?
sentences.zh: 万一它们来自地狱呢？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So the first thing to test, I suppose, is whether or not she is who she claims to be.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，首先要检验的事情是，她究竟是不是她所声称的那个人。

sentences.en: So, for example, is she a pucelle?
sentences.zh: 比如，她是一个处女吗？

sentences.en: Is she a maid?
sentences.zh: 她是一个纯洁的少女吗？

sentences.en: So they actually get two women at court, don't they, to examine her and to see whether or not she is, in fact, a virgin.
sentences.zh: 所以宫廷里实际上找了两个女人，对吧，来检查她，看看她实际上是不是处女。

sentences.en: And they say she is.
sentences.zh: 她们说她是。

sentences.en: So that's good news.
sentences.zh: 所以这是个好消息。

sentences.en: That is good news.
sentences.zh: 这确实是个好消息。

sentences.en: So they've checked out her physical condition and now they have to check out her kind of moral and spiritual condition.
sentences.zh: 所以他们检查了她的身体状况，现在他们必须检查她的道德和精神状况。

sentences.en: This is called the discretio spirituum.
sentences.zh: 这被称为辨别诸灵。

sentences.en: And they send her off.
sentences.zh: 然后他们把她打发走了。

sentences.en: Basically, they send her off for a viva, a PhD viva.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们送她去接受一场答辩，一场博士论文答辩。

sentences.en: They do.
sentences.zh: 他们真的这么做了。

sentences.en: Well, it's kind of like a debrief, I guess.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这有点像是一次情况汇报，我猜。

sentences.en: So she's sent to Poitiers, not far from Chinon.
sentences.zh: 所以她被送往了离希农不远的普瓦捷。

sentences.en: And in Poitiers, there are all kinds of scholars and doctors from the University of Paris, which has always been the kind of the leading center of theology in Christendom.
sentences.zh: 在普瓦捷，有来自巴黎大学的各种学者和博士，巴黎大学历来是基督教世界神学的主要中心。

sentences.en: But lots of these scholars are refugees from the English.
sentences.zh: 但这些学者中有许多人都是为了躲避英格兰人而流亡至此的难民。

sentences.en: And so Poitiers is their kind of base.
sentences.zh: 因此普瓦捷可以说是他们的基地。

sentences.en: And among the scholars and doctors there and the prelates is the Archbishop of Reims, who is Charles's chancellor.
sentences.zh: 在当地的学者、博士以及高级神职人员中，有兰斯大主教，他同时也是查理的宰相。

sentences.en: And so he puts himself at the head of the investigation into Joan.
sentences.zh: 于是他亲自领导了对贞德的调查。

sentences.en: And they, more than anyone, even more than the king, is alert to the risks.
sentences.zh: 他们比任何人都更清楚其中的风险，甚至比国王还要警惕。

sentences.en: So to quote Helen Castor, friend of the show, author of a wonderful book on Joan of Arc.
sentences.zh: 借用本节目老朋友、圣女贞德精彩传记作者海伦·卡斯特的话来说：

sentences.en: Female visionaries in the church's recent history had experienced their revelations when they were already under the care of a spiritual advisor.
sentences.zh: 教会近代史上的女性先知在获得神圣启示时，通常已经接受了某位心灵导师的照顾。

sentences.en: So this was true of Catherine of Siena, a confessor, perhaps, who could testify to their morals and the nature of their claiMs.
sentences.zh: 锡耶纳的凯瑟琳就是如此，她有一位神父之类的告解神父，可以为她们的道德以及她们所称的事实的性质作证。

sentences.en: Joan, by contrast, had appeared alone apart from her escort of armed men.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，贞德出现时孤身一人，除了护送她的武装士兵外别无他人。

sentences.en: And rather than simply conveying a message from heaven, she, a teenage girl, wanted to lead the king's troops into battle.
sentences.zh: 她不仅仅是传递来自天堂的信息，身为一个十几岁的女孩，她还想带领国王的军队冲锋陷阵。

sentences.en: And so this does make her exceptional.
sentences.zh: 这确实使她显得非同寻常。

sentences.en: Nothing really like Joan has been seen before.
sentences.zh: 历史上从未出现过真正类似贞德的人物。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: To repeat, she's wearing male clothes and that she absolutely insists on wearing them.
sentences.zh: 重申一遍，她穿着男装，而且她绝对坚持要穿男装。

sentences.en: And then on top of that, there's the styling of these male clothes.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，这些男装的款式也很有讲究。

sentences.en: They're not drab.
sentences.zh: 它们可不单调乏味。

sentences.en: Joan clearly is a bit of a fashionista.
sentences.zh: 贞德显然有点时尚达人的潜质。

sentences.en: She loves exactly the kind of expensive male clothing that moralists at the time are very down on.
sentences.zh: 她偏爱当时道德家们极其反感的昂贵男式服装。

sentences.en: So this also is a cause of anxiety.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是一个让人感到焦虑的原因。

sentences.en: But the people in Poitiers say, no, she's okay.
sentences.zh: 但普瓦捷的人们说，不，她没问题。

sentences.en: She has conversed with everyone publicly and privately, but no evil is found in her.
sentences.zh: 她公开和私下里与所有人都交谈过，但在她身上没有发现任何邪恶。

sentences.en: Only goodness, humility, virginity, piety, integrity and simplicity.
sentences.zh: 只有善良、谦逊、贞洁、虔诚、正直和纯朴。

sentences.en: I have to say they're making it sound absolutely awful.
sentences.zh: 我得说，他们把她形容得听起来糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: And her clothing, they say that's fine too, because actually Christ has kind of superseded Deuteronomy.
sentences.zh: 至于她的衣着，他们说那也没问题，因为实际上基督在某种程度上已经超越了《申命记》。

sentences.en: And actually, you know, Deuteronomy doesn't really apply to a woman who's been sent by God to lead men in war to recapture Orléans from the English.
sentences.zh: 而且实际上，你知道的，《申命记》并不真正适用于一个被上帝派遣来率领军队从英格兰人手中收复奥尔良的女性。

sentences.en: So it's kind of fine.
sentences.zh: 所以这算是没问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because basically the scholars too want to believe in it.
sentences.zh: 因为基本上学者们也希望相信这一点。

sentences.en: You know, they're desperate to see the English thrown out.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们迫切希望能看到英格兰人被赶走。

sentences.en: And also, of course, they know what the Dauphin wants.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们也很清楚王储想要什么。

sentences.en: And so essentially they're serving it up to him.
sentences.zh: 所以从本质上讲，他们是在投其所好。

sentences.en: So this is their verdict, which they send back to the Dauphin.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们的裁决结果，他们把这个结果送回给了王储。

sentences.en: The king should not prevent Joan from going to Orléans with his soldiers, but should have her escorted there honorably, placing his faith in God.
sentences.zh: 国王不应阻止贞德与其士兵前往奥尔良，而应以荣誉护送她前往，并将信仰寄托于上帝。

sentences.en: So essentially they're saying, you know, take a punt on it.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上他们的意思是，你知道的，赌一把吧。

sentences.en: Let's see what happens.
sentences.zh: 让我们看看会发生什么。

sentences.en: And this is the point when Joan dictates the letter that we began with to the English, basically an ultimatum.
sentences.zh: 就在这个时候，贞德向英格兰人口授了我们开篇提到的那封信，基本上是一份最后通牒。

sentences.en: I'm on my way.
sentences.zh: 我要来了。

sentences.en: You'd better watch out.
sentences.zh: 你们最好小心点。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Although she doesn't at this point send it.
sentences.zh: 尽管她当时并没有把信寄出去。

sentences.en: She will send it later on, but it's there waiting to go.
sentences.zh: 她会在稍后将其寄出，但信已经写好随时待命了。

sentences.en: And so then from Poitiers, she rejoins the Dauphin who has moved from Chinon to Tor.
sentences.zh: 于是，她从普瓦捷出发，与已经从希农移驾图尔的王储重新会合。

sentences.en: Tor is on the Loire.
sentences.zh: 图尔位于卢瓦尔河畔。

sentences.en: And here in the full gaze of the court and therefore of France, the seal is set on her status as the potential redeemer of France.
sentences.zh: 在这里，在宫廷众目睽睽之下，也就是在全法国的注视下，她作为法国潜在救世主的地位终于盖棺定论。

sentences.en: And this happens in three ways.
sentences.zh: 这通过三种方式实现。

sentences.en: First of all, she submits to an intimate inspection, this time by Yolande.
sentences.zh: 首先，她接受了一次私密检查，这次是由约兰德进行的。

sentences.en: There's a lot of inspections.
sentences.zh: 检查可真不少。

sentences.en: Then there's a kind of mad pantomime at court where Joan arrives and she gets directed to a captain and told this is the Dauphin.
sentences.zh: 接着宫廷里上演了一场疯狂的哑剧，贞德到达后被引向某位将领，并被告知这位就是王储。

sentences.en: And then to someone who has just returned from Orléans and told, well, this is the Dauphin.
sentences.zh: 然后又被引向一个刚从奥尔良回来的人，并被告知，嗯，这位才是王储。

sentences.en: And she says, oh, no, no, no, it's not.
sentences.zh: 而她说，哦，不，不，不，不是他。

sentences.en: And she goes up to the real Dauphin.
sentences.zh: 然后她径直走向真正的王储。

sentences.en: But hold on, she's met the Dauphin, hasn't she?
sentences.zh: 但等等，她之前不是已经见过王储了吗？

sentences.en: She has.
sentences.zh: 她确实见过。

sentences.en: So it's a pantomime.
sentences.zh: 所以这纯粹是一场哑剧。

sentences.en: It's staged.
sentences.zh: 这是精心编排的。

sentences.en: It's clearly designed to illustrate both the inherent regality of the Dauphin and the ability of Joan to fathom it.
sentences.zh: 显然旨在向世人展示王储天生的王者之气，以及贞德洞察这种气质的能力。

sentences.en: That's the maddest thing in this story so far.
sentences.zh: 这是这个故事目前为止最疯狂的部分。

sentences.en: An identity parade when she's already met him.
sentences.zh: 在已经见过面的情况下还要搞一场辨认身份的游行。

sentences.en: No, it's not mad because it's a kind of pageant.
sentences.zh: 不，这并不疯狂，因为这是一种庆典般的表演。

sentences.en: It's a display making public to the court the role that both the king and Joan are going to play.
sentences.zh: 这是一种向宫廷公开展示国王和贞德各自将要扮演角色的公开展示。

sentences.en: And then something very weird and mysterious does happen, which is not normal at all.
sentences.zh: 然后发生了一件非常诡异且神秘的事情，这在平时是绝对不正常的。

sentences.en: He asks Joan for a sign.
sentences.zh: 他向贞德索要一个神迹。

sentences.en: Convince me.
sentences.zh: 说服我。

sentences.en: Reassure me that you have indeed come from God.
sentences.zh: 向我保证你确实是奉上帝之命而来。

sentences.en: And Joan gives it to him.
sentences.zh: 贞德答应了他。

sentences.en: But what this sign was remains veiled.
sentences.zh: 但这个神迹究竟是什么，至今仍是个谜。

sentences.en: It's not publicized.
sentences.zh: 它并未被公之于众。

sentences.en: And in due course, Joan will be asked about it at her trial.
sentences.zh: 在适当的时候，贞德在审判中会被问及此事。

sentences.en: And she will talk about it.
sentences.zh: 她也会谈到这件事。

sentences.en: But we will come to that later on.
sentences.zh: 但我们稍后再谈到那部分。

sentences.en: Oh, my word.
sentences.zh: 我的天哪。

sentences.en: That's tantalizing.
sentences.zh: 这太撩人心弦了。

sentences.en: Isn't that exciting?
sentences.zh: 难道不是很让人兴奋吗？

sentences.en: It is tantalizing.
sentences.zh: 确实很撩人心弦。

sentences.en: It's a complex issue.
sentences.zh: 这是一个复杂的问题。

sentences.en: But I think it's clear that the sign is accepted by the Dauphin.
sentences.zh: 但我认为很明显，王储接受了这个神迹。

sentences.en: The green light is given.
sentences.zh: 绿灯已经亮起。

sentences.en: Joan is ready to go to war.
sentences.zh: 贞德准备奔赴战场了。

sentences.en: So it's now late April.
sentences.zh: 现在已经是四月下旬。

sentences.en: And as she rides off, she is a magnificent sight.
sentences.zh: 当她骑马离去时，那景象蔚为壮观。

sentences.en: So she is wearing a full suit of white armor that has been handmade for her by the king's own armorer.
sentences.zh: 她穿着一套由国王御用工匠为她量身打造的全套白色盔甲。

sentences.en: She has a new sword, which had been found behind the altar of the church at Fierbois.
sentences.zh: 她有一把新剑，是在菲耶布瓦教堂的祭坛后面找到的。

sentences.en: And which Joan later would say that her voices had said would be found there.
sentences.zh: 贞德后来曾说，她听到的声音曾预言这把剑会在那里被找到。

sentences.en: So she had then sent messengers and they had discovered the sword.
sentences.zh: 于是她派去了信使，他们果然找到了这把剑。

sentences.en: And the sword is very mysterious.
sentences.zh: 这把剑非常神秘。

sentences.en: It's covered with rust, which magically falls away as soon as it's touched.
sentences.zh: 它布满铁锈，但只要一触碰，铁锈就会神奇地脱落。

sentences.en: And it reveals five crosses along the blade and on the edge are inscribed the words Jisoo and Maria.
sentences.zh: 剑刃上隐约显现出五个十字架，边缘则刻着“吉苏”和“玛丽亚”这两个词。

sentences.en: This, of course, is absolutely part of medieval romance.
sentences.zh: 这当然完全属于中世纪的浪漫传奇。

sentences.en: It's very Lord of the Rings.
sentences.zh: 很有《指环王》的感觉。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 你知道的，就像那把断剑之类的东西。

sentences.en: A great hero has to have a magical sword.
sentences.zh: 伟大的英雄必须配有一把神奇的宝剑。

sentences.zh: 而现在，圣女贞德也拥有了一把神奇的宝剑。

sentences.en: And she's got a very nice banner as well.
sentences.zh: 而且她还拥有了一面非常漂亮的旗帜。

sentences.en: People often like a kind of magic banner, don't they?
sentences.zh: 人们通常都很喜欢某种神奇的旗帜，不是吗？

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你说得倒轻巧。

sentences.zh: 这可是一面壮丽辉煌的旗帜。

sentences.zh: 它是用白色的丝绸制作而成的。

sentences.en: It's covered in golden fleur-de-lis.
sentences.zh: 上面绣满了金色的鸢尾花图案。

sentences.en: Again, the words Jisoo and Maria are stitched into it.
sentences.zh: 同样的，“吉苏”和“玛丽亚”这两个字也被缝在了上面。

sentences.en: And they appear alongside an image of Christ flanked by two angels.
sentences.zh: 它们出现在基督的画像旁，基督身旁则侍立着两位天使。

sentences.en: So it's a really splendid sight.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个极其壮观的景象。

sentences.en: She's on a black horse, which is a gift from the Duke of Alonso, who absolutely loves her.
sentences.zh: 她骑着一匹黑色的骏马，这是阿隆索公爵送给她的礼物，阿隆索公爵对她喜爱至极。

sentences.en: We've said that.
sentences.zh: 我们之前提到过这一点。

sentences.en: He'd seen her practicing in the lists that Sheenor had been so impressed that he gave her the best charger that he had in his stables.
sentences.zh: 他曾看她在演武场上练习，并对她留下了极深的印象，于是把马厩里最好的战马送给了她。

sentences.en: And again, I mean, how Joan had made herself so proficient at horsemanship is a kind of puzzle.
sentences.zh: 话说回来，贞德究竟是如何让自己的骑术变得如此精湛的，这本身就是一个谜。

sentences.en: It's a mystery.
sentences.zh: 这真是一个不解之谜。

sentences.en: And she is at the head of an entire military retinue now.
sentences.zh: 而现在，她正率领着整整一支军队随从出行。

sentences.en: And this is led by the man who will serve her as her squire, a guy who's a very experienced soldier called Jean Dolan.
sentences.zh: 这支队伍由一个将要充当她贴身侍从的人领导，他是一个名叫让·多兰的经验丰富的老兵。

sentences.en: And he's basically there not just to serve her, but to look after her and protect her to make sure she doesn't get captured.
sentences.zh: 他留在那里的目的不仅仅是侍奉她，更是为了照顾她、保护她，确保她不会被俘虏。

sentences.en: And what's going on in Orléans while this has been happening?
sentences.zh: 那么，在发生这一切的时候，奥尔良那边情况如何呢？

sentences.en: Because the Orléans has been besieged all this time.
sentences.zh: 因为奥尔良这座城市已经被围困了这么长时间。

sentences.en: So presumably the people there are getting increasingly desperate.
sentences.zh: 所以想必那里的人们越来越绝望了。

sentences.en: Well, the news from Orléans is very grim.
sentences.zh: 嗯，从奥尔良传来的消息非常严峻。

sentences.en: The garrison is depleted.
sentences.zh: 守军兵力已经消耗殆尽。

sentences.en: The supplies are running out, both ammunition and food.
sentences.zh: 物资正在耗尽，无论是弹药还是粮食。

sentences.en: And people are starting to starve.
sentences.zh: 人们已经开始挨饿了。

sentences.en: And so Joan's mission is to ride with a convoy of some 3,000 men that the Dauphin has has scrabbled together.
sentences.zh: 因此，贞德的任务是率领一支由王太子东拼西凑起来的大约三千人的车队同行。

sentences.en: He's found ammunition.
sentences.zh: 他找到了弹药。

sentences.en: He's found food.
sentences.zh: 他找到了食物。

sentences.en: He's put them in wagons.
sentences.zh: 他把这些东西装上了马车。

sentences.en: He's got a kind of herd of cattle.
sentences.zh: 他还弄来了一群牛。

sentences.en: And Joan is going to accompany this train and hopefully get to Orléans and relieve the siege in that way.
sentences.zh: 贞德将随这支队伍同行，希望能抵达奥尔良，并以此方式解围。

sentences.en: And so they set off.
sentences.zh: 于是他们出发了。

sentences.en: She's taking her role as God's messenger very seriously.
sentences.zh: 她非常认真地对待自己作为上帝信使的使命。

sentences.en: So all prostitutes have been banished.
sentences.zh: 因此，所有的妓女都被驱逐了。

sentences.en: There are priests singing hymns at the head of the convoy.
sentences.zh: 有神父在车队前方带头唱着圣歌。

sentences.en: Soldiers who are marching are urged to offer confession daily.
sentences.zh: 行军的士兵们被敦促每天都要进行忏悔。

sentences.en: And I can see from your face, Dominic, that you were thinking this is not the way to build men's morale.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，从你的表情我能看出，你觉得这不是重振士气的好办法。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 确实不是。

sentences.en: But actually, it seems that it does.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，它似乎确实起到了这个作用。

sentences.en: It seems to have inspired the men.
sentences.zh: 它似乎激励了士兵们。

sentences.en: And as they ride, their morale is palpably higher.
sentences.zh: 当他们骑马前进时，士气明显高涨了许多。

sentences.en: Okay, well, I'm glad I'm not in that army.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我很高兴我不在那支军队里。

sentences.en: That's all I'll say.
sentences.zh: 这就是我想说的全部。

sentences.en: Well, you know, horses for courses, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 人各有志嘛，多米尼克。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: You know, this is the 15th century.
sentences.zh: 要知道，这可是15世纪啊。

sentences.zh: 他们向奥尔良推进，并在4月28日傍晚抵达了那里。

sentences.zh: 但当他们到达那里，贞德生平第一次看到奥尔良时，她却发现了一个可怕的事实：她、她的战友们以及运送物资的车队都在

sentences.zh: 而绝大多数英国军队也都在北岸。

sentences.en: And Joan feels that she has come to attack the English.
sentences.zh: 贞德觉得她是来攻打英国人的。

sentences.zh: 那她为什么会在河的错误这一边呢？

sentences.zh: 这怎么会发生呢？

sentences.zh: 她是被法国将领们故意欺骗了吗？

sentences.zh: 天哪，真是个悬念迭起的发展。

sentences.zh: 我都快按捺不住了。

sentences.zh: 我太激动了。

sentences.zh: 休息之后回来，我们就会知道究竟出了什么问题，以及她为什么会身处河的对岸。

sentences.zh: 伟大博弈，英国与俄罗斯之间的战略较量。

sentences.zh: 那是1429年4月28日的傍晚。

sentences.en: She's on the bank of the Loire, which is broader than it is now.
sentences.zh: 她站在卢瓦尔河岸边，那里的河面比现在还要宽阔。

sentences.en: On the other side, she can see Orléans and the English.
sentences.zh: 在河对岸，她可以看到奥尔良城以及英国人。

sentences.zh: 她可以看到城堡、教堂的尖顶、城市的城墙。

sentences.zh: 所以，汤姆，她还能看到一座残破的桥梁的废墟。

sentences.zh: 桥拱已经被彻底摧毁了。

sentences.zh: 所以你只能看到那种桥墩之类的东西。

sentences.zh: 这座桥曾将城市与南岸的一座奥古斯丁小修道院连接起来。
