sentences.zh: 而图雷尔要塞现在成了英国人在南岸的主要据点。

sentences.en: So, directly facing Orléans is under the command of a guy called Sir William Glassdale, who, even though he is a knight, had begun his career as an archer.
sentences.zh: 因此，直接面对奥尔良的据点由一个名叫威廉·格拉斯代尔爵士的人指挥，他虽然是一名骑士，但其军旅生涯却是从弓箭手开始的。

sentences.en: A very proficient and formidable warrior.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常精干且令人生畏的战士。

sentences.en: And he has turned Les Tourelles into a kind of massive platform for artillery.
sentences.zh: 他把图雷尔要塞变成了一个巨大的火炮阵地。

sentences.en: And this artillery, you know, it's firing across the Loire.
sentences.zh: 这些火炮正在跨过卢瓦尔河进行轰击。

sentences.en: It's battering the walls of Orléans on the north bank.
sentences.zh: 它们在猛烈轰击北岸的奥尔良城墙。

sentences.en: And Glassdale is able to hurl abuse at the defenders of Orléans, kind of threatening them with, you know, he's going to slaughter the lot of them when he captures the city.
sentences.zh: 格拉斯代尔得以向奥尔良的守军叫骂侮辱，威胁他们说等他攻陷这座城市时，要将他们赶尽杀绝。

sentences.en: He's a notorious figure.
sentences.zh: 这是一个臭名昭著的人物。

sentences.en: So, there's Glassdale in Les Tourelles and it's a significant target, but Joan isn't really interested in it because she knows that the real action is on the north side.
sentences.zh: 所以，格拉斯代尔就在图雷尔要塞里，这是一个重要的目标，但贞德其实对它并不感兴趣，因为她知道真正的行动重心在北岸。

sentences.en: That's where the English have focused most of their efforts.
sentences.zh: 那是英国人集中了大部分兵力的地方。

sentences.en: On the north side, they've got three fortresses along the length of the Loire, kind of blocking off attempts to relieve the city by the river.
sentences.zh: 在北岸，沿着卢瓦尔河他们有三座要塞，以此来阻断通过水路为城市解围的企图。

sentences.en: And they've also got a great screen of fortresses on the western side of the city that runs from Loire up to a great forest north of Orléans.
sentences.zh: 他们还在城市的西侧建有一道宏大的要塞防线，从卢瓦尔河一直延伸到奥尔良以北的一片大森林。

sentences.en: So, that basically is kind of blocking off access from there.
sentences.zh: 所以，这基本上切断了从那个方向进入的通道。

sentences.en: Now, on the eastern side of Orléans, things are open.
sentences.zh: 现在，在奥尔良的东侧，情况是开放的。

sentences.en: So, that is an opportunity perhaps for the French.
sentences.zh: 因此，这或许对法军来说是一个机会。

sentences.en: And so, this is what they decide that they will do.
sentences.zh: 于是，这就是他们决定要做的事情。

sentences.en: They decide that they will go upriver, maybe six miles north of Orléans,
sentences.zh: 他们决定逆流而上，大约在奥尔良以北六英里处，

sentences.en: and there they will make a crossing and they will then come back and they will try and get into Orléans that way because there aren't that many English siege works blocking them.
sentences.zh: 在那里他们将渡过河，然后折返回来，试图以此方式进入奥尔良，因为那边没有那么多英国人的围城工事阻挡。

sentences.en: And the guy who comes up with this strategy is the guy who has been in command in Orléans and who has been rowed over to meet Joan and the relief force.
sentences.zh: 提出这个策略的人，正是之前一直在奥尔良指挥、并被划船接来会见贞德和救援部队的那个人。

sentences.en: And this is a very, very impressive man.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常了不起的人。

sentences.en: He is called Jean and he is also more impressively known as the Bastard of Orléans.
sentences.zh: 他叫让，人们更喜欢用一个令人肃然起敬的称号来称呼他——奥尔良的私生子。

sentences.en: And he's called this because he's the half-brother, the illegitimate half-brother of the Duke of Orléans who's in captivity in England, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 之所以被称为这个，是因为他是奥尔良公爵同父异母的私生兄弟，而奥尔良公爵当时正被关押在英国做人质，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this guy, the Bastard, he's 27.
sentences.zh: 这家伙，也就是这个私生子，当时27岁。

sentences.en: He's very formidable.
sentences.zh: 他非常强大骇人。

sentences.en: He's a serious person.
sentences.zh: 他是一个严肃认真的人。

sentences.en: He's a very experienced commander.
sentences.zh: 他是一位经验极其丰富的指挥官。

sentences.en: He's the Dauphin's cousin.
sentences.zh: 他是王太子的表亲。

sentences.en: And actually, one reason for his prominence is that he's the last man standing of the House of Orléans who's in a position to fight for the city of Orléans.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他之所以如此显赫，原因之一在于他是奥尔良家族唯一留存下来、且有能力为奥尔良城战斗的人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And there's an incredible painting of him.
sentences.zh: 有一幅关于他的不可思议的画作。

sentences.en: People could look him up.
sentences.zh: 人们可以去查查看。

sentences.en: I mean, it's such a realistic portrait.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一幅极其逼真的肖像画。

sentences.en: You look at it and you can absolutely imagine what he's like.
sentences.zh: 你看一眼，就能完全想象出他是个什么样的人。

sentences.en: Not the kind of person that you, I think, would want to get into an argument with.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他不是那种你想跟他争论的人。

sentences.en: But also clearly very smart.
sentences.zh: 但显然也非常聪明。

sentences.en: But Joan, it has to be said, is not impressed.
sentences.zh: 不过必须得说，贞德对他并不买账。

sentences.en: Despite the fact that the Bastard of Orléans is the cousin of the king himself, she roundly bollocks him.
sentences.zh: 尽管奥尔良的私生子是国王本人的表亲，她还是狠狠地训斥了他一顿。

sentences.en: Was it on your advice she demands that I've been brought here on this side of the river instead of going directly against Talbot and the English?
sentences.zh: 是不是听了你的建议，她才要求把我带到河的这一边，而不是直接去跟塔尔博特和英军正面交锋？

sentences.en: And John Talbot is the most feared of all the English commanders.
sentences.zh: 而约翰·塔尔博特是所有英国指挥官中最让人闻风丧胆的一个。

sentences.en: And the Bastard of Orléans, you know, he says, yeah, it's absolutely my decision.
sentences.zh: 奥尔良的巴斯塔德，你知道的，他说，对，这完全是我的决定。

sentences.en: And Joan is very angry.
sentences.zh: 而且贞德非常生气。

sentences.en: She's very hurt.
sentences.zh: 她受到了很大的伤害。

sentences.en: She says, I have brought you the best reinforcement that any soldier or city ever had, the support of the king of heaven.
sentences.zh: 她说，我给你们带来了任何士兵或城市都拥有过的最好的增援，那就是来自天堂之王的支援。

sentences.en: And I think, Dominic, that at this point, you can imagine the Bastard of Orléans pulling the kind of face that you even now are pulling.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我想此时此刻，你可以想象奥尔良的巴斯塔德正摆出那种你现在脸上正挂着的表情。

sentences.en: Not wrong.
sentences.zh: 没说错。

sentences.en: But they have another council of war the next morning, don't they?
sentences.zh: 但第二天早上他们又开了一次军事会议，对吧？

sentences.en: And once again, she starts ranting and raving about how she wants to go on to the attack straight away.
sentences.zh: 她又一次开始喋喋不休、大发雷霆，说她想立刻发起进攻。

sentences.en: She's very basble about it.
sentences.zh: 她对此感到非常急不可耐。

sentences.en: You know, let's just attack.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就是直接进攻吧。

sentences.en: But again, she's ignored because the priority is to get the supplies across to the city.
sentences.zh: 但她再次被无视了，因为当务之急是将物资运送进城。

sentences.en: And so the Bastard's plan that they will go upriver.
sentences.zh: 所以巴斯塔德的计划是他们将逆流而上。

sentences.en: This is now everyone, apart from Joan, says, yes, this is a great idea.
sentences.zh: 除了贞德之外，现在所有人都觉得，好，这主意太棒了。

sentences.en: And so that's what they do.
sentences.zh: 于是他们就这样做了。

sentences.en: And so the plan is that they will go there and they will load the supplies onto barges.
sentences.zh: 他们的计划是去到那里，将物资装上驳船。

sentences.en: And then the barges will go back and take the food to Orléans.
sentences.zh: 然后驳船再返回，把食物运送到奥尔良。

sentences.en: But when they get there, absolute disaster.
sentences.zh: 但当他们到达那里时，简直是一场灾难。

sentences.en: The current is obviously against the barges, but so too is the wind, which is very, very strong, almost gale force.
sentences.zh: 水流显然与驳船前行的方向相反，风向也是如此，风非常非常大，几乎达到了狂风的级别。

sentences.en: And it's preventing the barges from reaching the French supply force.
sentences.zh: 这阻碍了驳船与法军补给部队会合。

sentences.en: So what does Joan do?
sentences.zh: 那么贞德做了什么？

sentences.en: She kneels down.
sentences.zh: 她跪了下来。

sentences.en: She prays to God to change the course of the wind.
sentences.zh: 她祈求上帝改变风向。

sentences.en: And Dominic, miraculously, the wind changes.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，奇迹般地，风向真的变了。

sentences.en: Yeah, that is a miracle.
sentences.zh: 没错，这真是一个奇迹。

sentences.en: I mean, winds never change otherwise, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，风平时怎么可能会变，对吧？

sentences.en: The Bastard of Orléans is convinced.
sentences.zh: 奥尔良的巴斯塔德被说服了。

sentences.en: And from this point on, he is persuaded that Joan has indeed been sent by God.
sentences.zh: 从这一刻起，他坚信贞德确实是上帝派来的。

sentences.en: So the supplies are loaded onto the barges.
sentences.zh: 于是物资被装上了驳船。

sentences.en: They're then sent back to Orléans.
sentences.zh: 随后它们被送回了奥尔良。

sentences.en: And 200 men at arms with Joan now cross the River Loire to the north bank, but not the rest of the expedition, not the rest of the 3,000 men.
sentences.zh: 贞德带着两百名武装士兵现在穿过卢瓦尔河来到北岸，但远征军的其余人员并没有跟过来，那三千人里剩下的大多没有来。

sentences.en: They instead turn around and head back to Blois, downriver from Orléans, which is their base.
sentences.zh: 他们反而转过身，朝奥尔良下游、作为他们基地的布卢瓦折返。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the reason for this, and again, Joan is upset about this because she had imagined that these soldiers had been sent to take on the English.
sentences.zh: 原因在于此——而且贞德对此又感到很不高兴，因为她原本以为这些士兵是被派去迎战英军的。

sentences.en: But this turns out not to have been the case at all.
sentences.zh: 但结果根本不是这么回事。

sentences.en: So again, she's absolutely steaming.
sentences.zh: 所以她再次气得火冒三丈。

sentences.en: However, now she's on the north bank.
sentences.zh: 不过，现在她已经在北岸了。

sentences.en: She is able to ride back the six miles and get to Orléans because, as we said, there aren't really many English fortresses in the way.
sentences.zh: 她能够骑马走回那六英里并抵达奥尔良，因为正如我们所说，路上其实并没有多少英国人的要塞。

sentences.en: So the English have not been able to cut it off completely.
sentences.zh: 所以英军没能彻底切断这条通路。

sentences.en: So they've left gaps in the eaSt.
sentences.zh: 因此他们在东面留下了缺口。

sentences.en: They haven't got enough men.
sentences.zh: 他们的人手不够。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And she's able to just ride straight in, basically, isn't she?
sentences.zh: 基本上她可以直接骑马冲进去，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so she makes a triumphant entry into the city.
sentences.zh: 于是她凯旋入城。

sentences.en: She's got her page preceding her, carrying her great silken banner.
sentences.zh: 她的侍童走在前面，举着她那面巨大的丝绸旗帜。

sentences.en: She's flanked on one side by the Bastard of Orléans, but also on the other by one of the most formidable of all the French captains,
sentences.zh: 她的一侧是奥尔良的巴斯塔德陪伴，另一侧则是所有法国指挥官中最令人畏惧的人物之一，

sentences.en: a guy known by the English and, indeed, by the French as Laire, who is a man of very humble origins.
sentences.zh: 一个无论在英国人还是法国人中间都被称为拉海尔的家伙，他出身非常卑微。

sentences.en: He's lame because he had a spectacular accident when the chimney of a pub fell on his legs.
sentences.zh: 他有些跛脚，因为曾发生过一起惊险的事故，一家酒馆的烟囱砸到了他的腿上。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: It hasn't stopped him from forging a very impressive reputation for himself.
sentences.zh: 但这并没有妨碍他为自己赢得令人瞩目的声誉。

sentences.en: And, in fact, his name, Laire, seems to have come from the Latin,
sentences.zh: 事实上，他的名字“拉海尔”，似乎源自拉丁语，

sentences.en: Irridae, the wrath of God, which is the nickname that the English give him.
sentences.zh: 意为“上帝的愤怒”，这也是英国人给他的绰号。

sentences.en: Yeah, like the friend of the show, Lope de Aguirre.
sentences.zh: 对，就像节目的老朋友洛佩·德·阿吉雷那样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: He's a menacing figure as well.
sentences.zh: 他也是个极具压迫感的人物。

sentences.en: And there he is by the side of Joan.
sentences.zh: 他就站在贞德身旁。

sentences.en: Joan, of course, is delighted by the reception she gets.
sentences.zh: 当然，贞德对她受到的欢迎感到非常高兴。

sentences.en: You know, she's being cheered and saluted as the saviour of Orléans.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她受到人们的欢呼和致敬，被视为奥尔良的救星。

sentences.en: But she knows that she still has lots to do, chief of which is persuading the Bastard of Orléans and Laire that they should go on the offensive and attack the English.
sentences.zh: 但她知道自己还有很多事情要做，其中最主要的就是说服奥尔良的巴斯塔德和拉海尔，让他们转入进攻并袭击英军。

sentences.en: The Bastard and Laire say, we can't because we haven't got enough men.
sentences.zh: 巴斯塔德和拉海尔说，我们做不到，因为我们人手不够。

sentences.en: We still haven't got enough men.
sentences.zh: 我们的人数依然不够。

sentences.en: And the people of Orléans, seeing Joan's escort, how few it is in number, only 200 men rather than the thousands they've been hoping for, they also, like Joan, are very downcaSt.
sentences.zh: 奥尔良的人民看到贞德的护卫队时，发现人数是如此之少，只有两百人，而不是他们期望中的成千上万，于是他们也和贞德一样，感到非常沮丧。

sentences.en: And despite their delight at getting food supplies and extra ammunition,
sentences.zh: 尽管他们对得到了食物补给和额外弹药感到高兴，

sentences.en: they almost immediately plunge back into a deep despond.
sentences.zh: 但他们几乎立刻又陷入了深深的绝望之中。

sentences.en: And there's a sense that barely hours after Joan has arrived, morale is, in a sense, even worse than it had been before Joan arrived.
sentences.zh: 人们甚至觉得，就在贞德抵达后区区几个小时里，士气在某种程度上比贞德到来之前还要糟糕。

sentences.en: And Joan and the Bastard of Orléans respond to this crisis in their own distinctive ways.
sentences.zh: 而贞德和奥尔良的巴斯塔德以各自独特的方式应对了这场危机。

sentences.en: So Joan's approach is to send a letter to Talbot and the English commanders.
sentences.zh: 所以贞德的方法是给塔尔博特和英国指挥官们写了一封信。

sentences.en: And of course, she had already sent Talbot a letter, that letter, Dominic, that you read out at the beginning of the show.
sentences.zh: 当然，她之前已经给塔尔博特写过一封信了，多米尼克，就是你在节目开头念的那封信。

sentences.en: The Herald who had taken that letter had been held captive by Talbot, which is very poor form.
sentences.zh: 送信的使者被塔尔博特扣押了，这做法实在很不地道。

sentences.en: That's not the kind of thing that you should do with Heralds.
sentences.zh: 这不是对待使者该有的行为。

sentences.en: And so Joan is very angry about this.
sentences.zh: 因此贞德对此非常生气。

sentences.en: And in the second letter, she demands that he release the Herald, that she give up the siege,
sentences.zh: 在第二封信中，她要求他释放使者，放弃围城，

sentences.en: and that he and all the rest of the English retire from Orléans and go back to England.
sentences.zh: 并且要求他以及所有其他英国人撤出奥尔良，返回英国。

sentences.en: Talbot, when he gets this letter, says, all right, I'm going to release the Herald.
sentences.zh: 塔尔博特收到这封信后说，好吧，我打算释放使者。

sentences.en: But he also sends Joan a message with this Herald saying, you are a whore.
sentences.zh: 但他也通过这名使者给贞德带话称，你不过是个妓女。

sentences.en: You should return to herding livestock.
sentences.zh: 你还是回去放牧吧。

sentences.en: If you don't, you are going to be burned as a witch.
sentences.zh: 如果你不这么做，你就会被当成女巫烧死。

sentences.en: And Joan, of course, is absolutely outraged by this.
sentences.zh: 当然，贞德对此感到无比愤怒。

sentences.en: And so she climbs up onto the battlements overlooking the Loire, and she shouts out to the English in Le Torel, the great fortress on the south side,
sentences.zh: 于是她爬上俯瞰卢瓦尔河的城墙，向南岸大要塞托雷勒里的英军大声喊话，

sentences.en: telling them to surrender, and they also reply with insults.
sentences.zh: 叫他们投降，而对方也用侮辱的话语回敬。

sentences.en: And specifically, they say, well, why would we surrender to a whore and her pimps?
sentences.zh: 他们具体说道，哼，我们凭什么向一个妓女和她的皮条客投降？

sentences.en: You are all toaSt.
sentences.zh: 你们这群人都死定了。

sentences.en: So that's Joan's approach.
sentences.zh: 这就是贞德的方法。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: The Bastard of Orléans' approach.
sentences.zh: 再看奥尔良巴斯塔德的方法。

sentences.en: He decides, actually, maybe Joan has a point.
sentences.zh: 他觉得，其实，也许贞德说得有道理。

sentences.en: Maybe there is no point in just trying to kind of string the siege along.
sentences.zh: 也许继续这么死拖着围城已经毫无意义了。

sentences.en: Maybe we really do have to stake everything on a single throw.
sentences.zh: 也许我们真的必须把一切都押在最后一搏上。

sentences.en: No, because if we don't, then the city is going to fall.
sentences.zh: 没错，因为如果我们不这么做，这座城市就会沦陷。

sentences.en: And so on the 1st of May, he leaves Orléans and he rides to Blois as fast as he possibly can.
sentences.zh: 所以在5月1日，他离开奥尔良，以最快的速度骑马赶往布卢瓦。

sentences.en: And when he gets there, he persuades all the various captains who were gathered there that they need to return with him to Orléans, because unless they do,
sentences.zh: 当他到达那里时，他极力说服聚集在那里的各位将领，他们必须随他一起返回奥尔良，因为除非他们这么做，

sentences.en: then the city is definitely going to be loSt.
sentences.zh: 否则这座城市就真的保不住了。

sentences.en: And this time he decides he's not going to go along the south bank.
sentences.zh: 这一次他决定不再走南岸。

sentences.en: He's going to go along the north bank.
sentences.zh: 他要走北岸。

sentences.en: So directly towards the English siege positions where they're strongeSt.
sentences.zh: 也就是直接朝着英军布防最坚固的围城阵地前进。

sentences.en: In other words, he basically has adopted Joan's plan.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他基本上采用了贞德的计划。

sentences.en: And this plan, of course, because the siege, like the English siege lines are at their strongest, means that he is probably going to have to fight his way through.
sentences.zh: 当然，由于英军的围城防线最为坚固，这个计划意味着他可能不得不强行杀出一条血路。

sentences.en: So on the 3rd of May, the Bastard leaves Blois.
sentences.zh: 因此在5月3日，巴斯塔德离开了布卢瓦。

sentences.en: He's got another huge train of wagons full of ammunition and food and stuff.
sentences.zh: 他还带着另一支装满弹药、食物和其他物资的庞大车队。

sentences.en: And the following day, he approaches the English lines on the western flank of Orléans.
sentences.zh: 第二天，他接近了位于奥尔良西翼的英军防线。

sentences.en: Well, they're kind of fortresses, siege positions and so on.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也就是那些要塞、围城阵地之类的东西。

sentences.en: Simultaneously, as he approaches the siege lines, a squad of 500 horsemen led by La Hyre and accompanied by Joan with her splendid banner, sally out from Orléans to meet them.
sentences.zh: 就在他接近围城阵地的同时，由拉海尔率领、并有打着华丽旗帜的贞德同行的五百名骑兵小队，从奥尔良出城与他们会合。

sentences.en: They are, of course, absolutely expecting that the English will be there and that there will be a battle.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们完全料到英军会在那里并会爆发一场战斗。

sentences.en: But in the event, the English don't try to stop them.
sentences.zh: 但在实际情况中，英军并没有试图阻拦他们。

sentences.en: The Bastard of Orléans and his men are able to pass through the siege lines.
sentences.zh: 奥尔良的巴斯塔德及其部下得以顺利穿过围城防线。

sentences.en: They meet up with the horsemen led by La Hyre and accompanied by Joan.
sentences.zh: 他们与拉海尔率领并有贞德同行的骑兵会合了。

sentences.en: And together, in a mood of absolute triumph, they head to Orléans, they enter the city and there they are.
sentences.zh: 然后他们怀着绝对胜利的心情一同前往奥尔良，进入了这座城市，这就是当时的情形。

sentences.en: They haven't had to fight.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至不需要战斗。

sentences.en: And the reason for this is basically because, and we've touched on it before, the English don't have quite enough men to make the investment of Orléans absolute.
sentences.zh: 之所以会这样，基本上是因为——我们之前也提到过——英国人没有足够多的人手来对奥尔良实施绝对合围。

sentences.en: There are about 4,000 of them.
sentences.zh: 他们大约有四千人。

sentences.en: And these 4,000 men have to occupy a series of fortresses that are scattered all around Orléans, including, of course, La Torelle on the South Bank.
sentences.zh: 这四千人必须驻守散布在奥尔良周边的各个要塞，当然也包括南岸的托雷勒要塞。

sentences.en: I have to say, Tom, it's really striking you make this point.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我不得不说，你提出这一点真的很引人注目。

sentences.en: So the siege of Orléans, the relief of Orléans is often seen as this sort of miraculous underdog victory against all the odds.
sentences.zh: 所以，奥尔良之围的解围，通常被视为在逆境中某种创造奇迹的弱者胜利。

sentences.en: But actually, if there's only 4,000 English, I mean, when you think of all the battles we've done
sentences.zh: 但实际上，如果英国人只有四千人的话，我的意思是，回想一下我们做过的所有战役，

sentences.en: and the rest is history, I'm not talking about the World Wars and so on, but I don't know, the Great Northern War or something.
sentences.zh: 以及其他历史事件，我不是指世界大战之类的，但怎么说呢，比如大北方战争什么的。

sentences.en: You know, these numbers are pretty small, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些数字其实很小，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, by the standards of some wars, this is a skirmish rather than a battle.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，以某些战争的标准来看，这只是一场小冲突，算不上真正的战役。

sentences.en: Not by the standards of the Hundred Years' War.
sentences.zh: 以百年战争的标准来看并非如此。

sentences.en: I mean, 4,000 is a really substantial force, and it would certainly be a substantial force in a pitched battle.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，四千人是一支相当庞大的军队，在阵地战中绝对算得上一支主力部队。

sentences.en: But Orléans is a large city.
sentences.zh: 但奥尔良是一座大城市。

sentences.en: So there just aren't quite enough.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的人数确实不太够。

sentences.en: And also, there is a kind of a backup force that had been stationed by the English for just such an eventuality, but the messengers don't reach it in time.
sentences.zh: 而且，英国人原本为了应付这种情况驻扎了一支后备部队，但信使没能及时赶到。

sentences.en: And so that's a piece of luck.
sentences.zh: 所以这也算是一种运气。

sentences.en: And the consequence of this is that basically the French numbers now match the English.
sentences.zh: 其结果就是，法军的人数现在基本上和英军持平了。

sentences.en: The French now have about 4,000 men as well.
sentences.zh: 法军现在也有大约四千人。

sentences.en: Yeah, and the English are fighting on foreign soil as well, so they've really got it all to do.
sentences.zh: 对，而且英国人是在异国他乡作战，所以他们确实面临着极大的挑战。

sentences.en: Well, but also they're scattered in all these fortresses, whereas the French are concentrated in a single place.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且他们分散在各个要塞里，而法军则集中在一个地方。

sentences.en: And so this is, you know, this is a key moment.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，这是一个关键时刻。

sentences.en: And so now, Joan, when she says to the Bastard of Olyon, lay here, come on, let's have a crack.
sentences.zh: 于是现在，当贞德对奥尔良的巴斯塔德和拉海尔说，来吧，我们去干一场吧。

sentences.en: Let's get on with it.
sentences.zh: 我们上吧。

sentences.en: They say, yeah, fine.
sentences.zh: 他们回答说，好，行。

sentences.en: Okay, let's.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那就上。

sentences.en: And so that same afternoon that the Bastard of Olyon has arrived in Olyon, they decide to attack the softest English target available to them, which is a very isolated fortress
sentences.zh: 就在奥尔良的巴斯塔德抵达奥尔良的那个下午，他们决定进攻他们能找到的防守最薄弱的英国目标，那是一座非常孤立的要塞，

sentences.en: east of Olyon on the North Bank.
sentences.zh: 位于奥尔良以东的北岸。

sentences.en: So basically, there aren't any kind of other English soldiers ready to hand.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，附近没有什么其他随时待命的英军士兵。

sentences.en: The garrison in that fortress is on its own.
sentences.zh: 那个要塞里的守军只能孤军奋战。

sentences.en: And so the French launch a full-scale attack against this fortress, and it falls after three hours of very hard fighting.
sentences.zh: 于是法军对这座要塞发起了全面进攻，经过三个小时的苦战，要塞陷落了。

sentences.en: The English, you'll be pleased to hear, put up a very good show.
sentences.zh: 你听了可能会高兴，英国人表现得非常顽强。

sentences.en: Of course they do.
sentences.zh: 他们当然会这样。

sentences.en: And this is Joan's first experience of battle.
sentences.zh: 这也是贞德第一次经历战斗。

sentences.en: She doesn't actually fight herself.
sentences.zh: 她其实并没有亲自参战。

sentences.en: You know, she never actually draws a sword.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她从没有真正拔剑相向。

sentences.en: She never kills anyone.
sentences.zh: 她从没有杀死任何人。

sentences.en: But she is absolutely in the battle line, brandishing her banner, urging the French on.
sentences.zh: 但她确实身处战线之中，挥舞着旗帜，激励着法军。

sentences.en: And at the end of the, when the fortress has been captured, blood is flowing.
sentences.zh: 在战斗结束时，当要塞被攻占后，鲜血直流。

sentences.en: You know, she sees this for the first time.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她这是生平第一次亲眼见到这种景象。

sentences.en: And so she broods on it that evening, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想那天晚上她一直在对此沉思。

sentences.en: And the next day she makes yet another call on the English to surrender.
sentences.zh: 第二天，她再次呼吁英国人投降。

sentences.en: So again, she writes her third letter to them.
sentences.zh: 于是，她又给他们写了第三封信。

sentences.en: You men of England who have no right to this kingdom of France, the king of heaven orders and commands you through me, Joan the maid, to abandon your strongholds and go back to
sentences.zh: 你们这些英格兰人，对法兰西王国毫无权利，天国的君主通过我——圣女贞德命令并要求你们：放弃你们的据点，回到

sentences.en: your own country.
sentences.zh: 你们自己的国家去。

sentences.en: If not, I will make a war cry that will be remembered forever.
sentences.zh: 如果不从，我会发出一个让人永远铭记的战斗怒吼。

sentences.en: I am writing this to you for the third and last time.
sentences.zh: 这是我第三次也是最后一次写信给你们。

sentences.en: I will write no more.
sentences.zh: 我不会再写了。

sentences.en: And she ties the letter to an arrow and has it fired into the English camp.
sentences.zh: 接着，她把信绑在箭上，让人射进了英格兰人的军营。

sentences.en: And the response is the familiar one.
sentences.zh: 而回应则是大家意料之中的。

sentences.en: Basically, piss off, you whore.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是：滚开，你这个婊子。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Armagnac whore, they call her.
sentences.zh: 他们叫她阿马尼亚克的婊子。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 真有趣。

sentences.en: A reminder that there is an element of a civil war to this, as well as a war between the French and the English, right?
sentences.zh: 这提醒了我们，除了法兰西和英格兰之间的战争，这里面其实也有内战的成分，对吧？

sentences.en: Burgundians and Armagnacs.
sentences.zh: 勃艮第派和阿马尼亚克派。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So the English clearly are not going to withdraw.
sentences.zh: 所以英格兰人显然是不打算撤退的。

sentences.en: And so Joan and the French captains decide, well, we're going to continue attacking them.
sentences.zh: 于是贞德和法兰西的将领们决定：好吧，我们要继续攻击他们。

sentences.en: And so on dawn the next day, which is the 6th of May, Joan makes confession.
sentences.zh: 所以在第二天也就是5月6日的黎明，贞德做了忏悔。

sentences.en: She hears mass.
sentences.zh: 她听了弥撒。

sentences.en: And then she joins hundreds of French soldiers who are clambering into boats, crossing the
sentences.zh: 然后她加入了成百上千法兰西士兵的行列，他们挤进小船，

sentences.en: Loire in a great flotilla to an island in the middle of the river.
sentences.zh: 乘着庞大的船队渡过卢瓦尔河，来到河中央的一座岛屿。

sentences.en: And then from that island, a pontoon is made out of the bridges and soldiers start crossing it onto the south bank.
sentences.zh: 接着从那座岛开始，人们用浮桥连接起来，士兵们开始经此渡向南岸。

sentences.en: And the goal of this operation is to flush the English out of the great Augustinian priory
sentences.zh: 这次行动的目标是将英格兰人从宏大的奥古斯丁小修道院

sentences.en: and the tower of Le Torel so that they will then be cleared pretty completely from the southern bank.
sentences.zh: 以及图雷尔之塔中赶出去，从而将他们从南岸彻底清除干净。

sentences.en: And Glasdale, the ex-archer, the captain of Le Torel, will no longer be able to menace
sentences.zh: 这样，前弓箭手、图雷尔之塔的指挥官格拉斯代尔，

sentences.en: Orléans with his artillery.
sentences.zh: 就再也无法用他的火炮威胁奥尔良了。

sentences.en: And Joan is on the southern bank, isn't she?
sentences.zh: 而贞德当时就在南岸，对吧？

sentences.en: She's with all her cronies.
sentences.zh: 她和她所有的亲信在一起。

sentences.en: So there's the bastard.
sentences.zh: 所以有私生子在。

sentences.en: There's that bloke, Laire, the wrath of God.
sentences.zh: 还有那个号称“上帝之怒”的家伙拉海尔。

sentences.en: And there's a third guy.
sentences.zh: 还有第三个人。

sentences.en: Now, I always think you should judge somebody by the company they keep.
sentences.zh: 现在，我一直认为你应该通过一个人结交的朋友来判断他是什么样的人。

sentences.en: And this is a lord from Brittany.
sentences.zh: 这是一位来自布列塔尼的领主。

sentences.en: And he's got quite a reputation, hasn't he, for all kinds of activities.
sentences.zh: 他在各种活动中可谓“名声在外”，不是吗？

sentences.en: And he is called Gilles de Rey.
sentences.zh: 他名叫吉尔·德·雷.

sentences.en: Well, at this point, Dominic, he has a reputation as a very proficient guerrilla leader.
sentences.zh: 嗯，多米尼克，此时他在人们眼中是一个极具能力的游击战领袖。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: In due course, he will have a reputation for other things.
sentences.zh: 不过假以时日，他会因为其他事情而“闻名遐迩”。

sentences.en: And we may come to that in due course.
sentences.zh: 我们到时可能会聊到这一点。

sentences.en: But at this point, his reputation, like that of the Bastard of Orléans and Laire, is as a very proficient captain of men.
sentences.zh: 但在当时，他的名声和奥尔良的私生子以及拉海尔一样，是一位极具能力的带兵将领。

sentences.en: And so these three men, with Joan, are leading the attack on the English positions in the
sentences.zh: 因此，这三个人与贞德一起，领导了对英格兰人位于

sentences.en: Priory and Les Togrel.
sentences.zh: 小修道院和图雷尔阵地的进攻。

sentences.en: When the captains reach the Priory, they're right up against it.
sentences.zh: 当将领们抵达小修道院时，他们已经逼近了阵地。

sentences.en: And they think, oh, actually, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 他们心里想：哦，说实话，我可说不准。

sentences.en: I mean, this looks a bit quite a tough nut to crack.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这看起来似乎是个挺难啃的硬骨头。

sentences.en: And they think, oh, maybe we should delay.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得：哦，也许我们应该推迟进攻。

sentences.en: Maybe we should try and get some more reinforcements.
sentences.zh: 也许我们应该设法调集更多援军。

sentences.en: But Joan, she's not having any of it.
sentences.zh: 但贞德根本不听这一套。

sentences.en: She says, we've got this.
sentences.zh: 她说：我们能行。

sentences.en: We're ready to do it.
sentences.zh: 我们已经准备好开战了。

sentences.en: And Laire agrees.
sentences.zh: 拉海尔也表示同意。

sentences.en: And so the whole mass of the French forces gathered in front of the Priory, they surge towards the walls of the Priory and they break over it.
sentences.zh: 于是，聚集在修道院前的大批法兰西军队向修道院的墙壁汹涌扑去，并成功突破了防线。

sentences.en: And even though the English fight bravely, the French are able to sweep them aside.
sentences.zh: 尽管英格兰人奋勇抵抗，法兰西人还是将他们横扫击溃。

sentences.en: They pile into the Priory itself.
sentences.zh: 他们蜂拥进入修道院内部。

sentences.en: The English withdraw and they retreat into the great tower of Les Torelles.
sentences.zh: 英格兰人见状撤退，退守到宏大的图雷尔高塔中。

sentences.en: And Joan, again, despite the fact that she has just trodden on the spike of a caltrap.
sentences.zh: 而贞德，尽管她刚刚踩到了一个铁蒺藜的尖刺——

sentences.en: So those are those kind of weapon, you know, those those kind of booby traps that they put to stop horses.
sentences.zh: 也就是那种用来阻止战马的武器，你知道的，那种诡雷类的东西。

sentences.en: So she's limping.
sentences.zh: 所以她现在一瘸一拐的。

sentences.en: But she doesn't care about that.
sentences.zh: 但她根本不在乎这个。

sentences.en: She's all for launching a massive attack.
sentences.zh: 她一心只想发动大规模的进攻。

sentences.en: But she is in pain.
sentences.zh: 然而她确实在忍受痛苦。

sentences.en: And so she's kind of they say the captain say, well, look, I think you should maybe retreat.
sentences.zh: 所以将领们就说：听着，我觉得你或许应该撤下去。

sentences.en: You know, go and have it tended to have a few plasters or whatever.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，去包扎一下伤口或者贴个膏药什么的。

sentences.en: And so she says, yeah, all right.
sentences.zh: 于是她说：好吧，行吧。

sentences.en: And so she withdraws to the camp.
sentences.zh: 接着她便退回了营地。

sentences.en: But once she's gone, the remaining captains, they hold a council of war and they agree that they don't actually have the numbers to attack Les Torelles.
sentences.zh: 但她一走，剩下的将领们便召开了军事会议，他们一致认为以目前的人数根本不足以进攻图雷尔。

sentences.en: They may have taken the Priory, but Les Torelles is just too formidable.
sentences.zh: 他们或许拿下了小修道院，但图雷尔实在是太难对付了。

sentences.en: You know, it's the largeSt.
sentences.zh: 要知道，那是最大的。

sentences.en: It's the most heavily defended fortress the English have.
sentences.zh: 那是英格兰人防御最严固的堡垒。

sentences.en: And therefore, it would be insane to launch an attack against it.
sentences.zh: 因此，对它发动进攻简直是疯了。

sentences.en: That's fair enough.
sentences.zh: 这倒也合情合理。

sentences.en: But Joan doesn't like that, does she?
sentences.zh: 但贞德可不乐意，对吧？

sentences.en: Because when she finds out about it that evening, she goes absolutely ballistic.
sentences.zh: 因为当她那天傍晚得知这个消息时，她气得简直要发疯。

sentences.en: And she says, come on, God wants us to do this.
sentences.zh: 她说：拜托，上帝希望我们这么做。

sentences.en: What are you thinking?
sentences.zh: 你们脑子里在想什么？

sentences.en: You need to change your mind.
sentences.zh: 你们必须改变主意。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And she says, you know, you captains, you've conferred among yourselves.
sentences.zh: 她说道：你们这些将领，你们自己商量过了。

sentences.en: But I, Joan, I have conferred with God.
sentences.zh: 但我，贞德，我可是和上帝商量过了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: So the next morning, there's another council of war and Joan succeeds in persuading, you know, changing their minds.
sentences.zh: 于是第二天早上，又召开了一次军事会议，贞德成功说服了他们，让他们改变了主意。

sentences.en: They say, yeah, all right.
sentences.zh: 他们说：好吧，行吧。

sentences.en: Okay, let's go for it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那就大举进攻吧。

sentences.en: And to quote Huizinga, the great Dutch historian we quoted in the previous episode, it is clear, I think, that it's tempting to think this is kind of a lunatic approach.
sentences.zh: 借用我们在上一集中引用过的大荷兰历史学家赫伊津花的观点，我认为显而易见的是，人们很容易觉得这是一种疯狂的做法。

sentences.en: She's just kind of saying attack, attack, attack, but I think it does touch something deep in the hearts of the French captains.
sentences.zh: 她只是一味地喊着进攻、进攻、进攻，但我认为这确实触及了法兰西将领们内心的深处。

sentences.en: You know, they sense a kind of a quality of heroism to it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们从中感受到了一种英雄主义的品质。

sentences.en: So to quote Huizinga, her courage and her confidence, these are the most immediate elements of her nature and the ones that give the most tangible explanation of her success.
sentences.zh: 正如赫伊津花所言：她的勇气和自信，是她天性中最直接的特质，也是对她成功最具说服力的诠释。

sentences.en: A greatness that manifests itself in a superior, irresistible, and infectious bravery.
sentences.zh: 那是一种展现为卓越、不可抗拒且极具感染力的勇敢之伟大。

sentences.en: And I think that infectious bravery, the captains pick up on it.
sentences.zh: 我想这种具有感染力的勇敢，深深感染了各位将领。

sentences.en: As a result, on the 7th of May, 1429, the fateful decision is taken to attack les Tourelles.
sentences.zh: 因此，在1429年5月7日，人们做出了决定命运的决定：进攻图雷尔。

sentences.en: And this is a decision that it may be determines the course of the Hundred Years' War.
sentences.zh: 这个决定或许决定了百年战争的走向。

sentences.en: So waves after waves of French attacks are launched on the Great Keep of Les Tourelles.
sentences.zh: 于是，一波又一波的法兰西攻击浪潮向图雷尔的主城堡发起了冲击。

sentences.en: The goal is to bridge the ditch that surrounds the tower with brushwood and then to bring ladders to put them on the side of the walls and to climb up.
sentences.zh: 他们的目标是用灌木填平环绕塔楼的壕沟，然后架起云梯靠在墙边爬上去。

sentences.en: Joan is with an attack party.
sentences.zh: 贞德和突击队在一起。

sentences.en: There's a ladder.
sentences.zh: 那里架着一架云梯。

sentences.en: She climbs up the ladder.
sentences.zh: 她顺着云梯往上爬。

sentences.en: And as she does so, she's hit in the neck by a crossbow bolt.
sentences.zh: 就在这时，她的脖子被一支弩箭击中了。

sentences.en: She's knocked backwards off the ladder and she drops her banner into the mud that's being churned up by all the men-at-arMs.
sentences.zh: 她从云梯上向后摔落，把军旗掉落在一群重甲骑兵践踏出的泥泞之中。

sentences.en: And so there's a great cheer goes up from the English.
sentences.zh: 于是英格兰人爆发出一阵巨大的欢呼声。

sentences.en: And obviously the morale of the French is pretty badly dented.
sentences.zh: 法兰西人的士气显然受到了相当沉重的打击。

sentences.en: Joan is led away.
sentences.zh: 贞德被扶了下去。

sentences.en: The French attack flags.
sentences.zh: 法兰西人的进攻势头减弱了。

sentences.en: The Bastard of Orléans decides, well, I think, you know, this attack isn't going to work.
sentences.zh: 奥尔良的私生子心想：好吧，我觉得这次进攻大概是行不通了。

sentences.en: We should call it off.
sentences.zh: 我们应该取消行动。

sentences.en: We'll wait for the morning.
sentences.zh: 等明天早上再说。

sentences.en: We'll bring over artillery from Orléans.
sentences.zh: 我们从奥尔良把火炮运过来。

sentences.en: We've got all this ammunition.
sentences.zh: 我们有这么多的弹药。

sentences.en: We'll have a crack again the next day.
sentences.zh: 明天再狠狠地打他们一次。

sentences.en: But Joan's squire, Jean Doulon, who is, you know, a big fan of Joan by this point, he picks up her banner.
sentences.zh: 但是贞德的随从让·多隆，此时已经成了贞德的狂热崇拜者，他捡起了她的旗帜。

sentences.en: He begins climbing up the ladder, still brandishing it.
sentences.zh: 他手里挥舞着旗帜，开始往云梯上爬。

sentences.en: You know, war cries left, right and center.
sentences.zh: 四面八方到处都是战斗的呐喊声。

sentences.en: All the other soldiers see this.
sentences.zh: 所有其他的士兵都看到了这一幕。

sentences.en: They start following Jean up his ladder.
sentences.zh: 他们开始跟着让爬上云梯。

sentences.en: They start putting up their own ladders.
sentences.zh: 他们开始架起自己的云梯。

sentences.en: They're all piling up.
sentences.zh: 所有人都蜂拥而上。

sentences.en: And Joan, who is standing on the edge of the ditch, yelling encouragement, she urges the Bastard, come on, we've got this.
sentences.zh: 而站在壕沟边缘大声鼓励大家的贞德，催促着私生子说：快来，我们能赢。

sentences.en: Let's renew the attack.
sentences.zh: 让我们重整旗鼓继续进攻。

sentences.en: And the Bastard of Orléans is persuaded.
sentences.zh: 奥尔良的私生子被说服了。

sentences.en: And so the attack continues.
sentences.zh: 于是战斗继续进行。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, on the far side of the river, the townsmen of Orléans have got these great wooden planks,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在河的对岸，奥尔良的市民们拿来了巨大的木板，

sentences.en: and they are laying these planks over the gap in the bridge that they demolished so that the arch is bridged.
sentences.zh: 他们把这些木板铺在之前被他们拆毁的桥梁缺口上，把桥拱连接起来。

sentences.en: And their aim is to cross this kind of makeshift bridge and attack Les Torelles from the opposite side to the attack that's being launched by Joan and the Bastard of Orléans,
sentences.zh: 他们的目标是穿过这座临时搭建的桥梁，从与贞德和奥尔良私生子进攻方向相反的一侧攻击图雷尔，

sentences.en: so that effectively the English in the keep will be completely surrounded.
sentences.zh: 这样城堡里的英格兰人就会彻底陷入合围。

sentences.en: And the English defenders, recognizing this, begin to panic, and their commander, this, you know, much feared, much hated, incredibly intimidating ex-archer, Sir William Glassdale,
sentences.zh: 英格兰守军见状开始惊慌失措，他们的指挥官——也就是那个备受畏惧、极其招人恨、威慑力十足的前弓箭手威廉·格拉斯代尔爵士，

sentences.en: he loses his footing, he plummets into the river, and of course he's weighed down by his armor, and so he sinks to the bottom.
sentences.zh: 脚底一滑，跌落河中，由于身披重甲不堪重负，他沉入了水底。

sentences.en: Oh no!
sentences.zh: 哦不！

sentences.en: That is the end of him.
sentences.zh: 他这下彻底完蛋了。

sentences.en: And with the loss of their commander, the English effectively give up, and they are massacred by the victorious French.
sentences.zh: 随着指挥官的阵亡，英格兰人彻底放弃了抵抗，并在胜利的法兰西人面前遭到屠杀。

sentences.en: 500 men in all are slaughtered.
sentences.zh: 总共有500人被屠戮一空。

sentences.en: And so by the evening, the Tower of Les Torelles, the Priory, both of them are in French hands, and the victors, rather than return to Orléans by boats,
sentences.zh: 因此到了傍晚，图雷尔之塔和小修道院双双落入法兰西人手中，胜利者们不再乘船返回奥尔良，

sentences.en: are able to return to the city across the wooden planks that have been laid across the river.
sentences.zh: 而是能够踩着横跨河面的木板直接返回城内。

sentences.en: And of course, you know, there's an absolute mood of ecstasy.
sentences.zh: 当然啦，现场弥漫着一种狂喜的情绪。

sentences.en: Bells are pealing, crowds are cheering, Joan is the heroine of the moment.
sentences.zh: 钟声敲响，人群欢呼，贞德成为了当之无愧的英雄。

sentences.en: And what about the English?
sentences.zh: 那英格兰人呢？

sentences.en: So the English back out in their kind of siege, their encampments and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 英格兰人退回到了他们的围城营地之类的地方。

sentences.en: So you've got Suffolk and Talbot and Scales, all these kind of hard-bitten captains, and they're pretty downcast now, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 萨福克、塔尔韦尔、斯凯尔斯，所有这些身经百战的将领们，现在都情绪低落，对吧？

sentences.en: Because they've lost a lot of men, they've lost their principal sort of forts for prosecuting the siege.
sentences.zh: 因为他们损失了大量兵力，失去了用以维持围城的关键堡垒。

sentences.en: They've also, crucially, lost control of the bridge and the river, so Orléans can now get supplies and reinforcements from the south.
sentences.zh: 更关键的是，他们失去了对桥梁和河流的控制，所以奥尔良现在可以从南部获得补给和增援了。

sentences.en: And basically, the game is up for them in Orléans, right?
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们在奥尔良的牌已经打完了，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They've got no prospect of success.
sentences.zh: 他们已经没有任何成功的希望了。

sentences.en: And the English commanders recognise this.
sentences.zh: 英格兰指挥官们也意识到了这一点。

sentences.en: Obviously, they're anxious to save face.
sentences.zh: 显然，他们急于挽回颜面。

sentences.en: And so Suffolk, the guy who's in overall command, he draws his men up in formation, essentially challenging the French to a pitched battle.
sentences.zh: 因此，总指挥萨福克将他的部下列成阵型，本质上是在向法兰西人下战书，要求进行决战。

sentences.en: But of course, you know, I mean, the French don't need to do it.
sentences.zh: 但当然啦，法兰西人根本没必要这么做。

sentences.en: They came here to relieve Orléans.
sentences.zh: 他们来这儿是为了解救奥尔良。

sentences.en: They've relieved it.
sentences.zh: 他们已经解围了。

sentences.en: So why would they risk losing it all again by taking on the English bowmen?
sentences.zh: 那他们为什么还要去招惹英格兰弓箭手，冒着把一切成果重新输掉的风险呢？

sentences.en: So an hour passes.
sentences.zh: 一个小时过去了。

sentences.en: The English give up.
sentences.zh: 英格兰人放弃了。

sentences.en: They turn around and they start marching northwards away from Orléans.
sentences.zh: 他们转过身，开始向北行军，撤离奥尔良。

sentences.en: And the siege is over.
sentences.zh: 围城战就这样结束了。

sentences.en: So the siege had lasted for six months.
sentences.zh: 因此，这场围城战持续了六个月。

sentences.en: But in four days, Joan and the French had been able to relieve the city.
sentences.zh: 但在四天之内，贞德和法军就成功解除了对这座城市的围困。

sentences.en: And to the Dauphin and to those who support him, this seems like, you know, she's delivered on her promises.
sentences.zh: 对于王太子和支持他的人来说，这看起来就像是，你知道的，她兑现了自己的承诺。

sentences.en: The miracle from God was foretold and it has duly arrived.
sentences.zh: 上帝的奇迹曾被预言，如今也如期降临。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, it absolutely strikes the Dauphin and everybody who supports him as a miracle.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，王太子和所有支持他的人绝对把这当作一个奇迹。

sentences.en: This victory seems to have come from nowhere.
sentences.zh: 这场胜利似乎凭空出现。

sentences.en: Soldiers whose morale was at rock bottom now seem, you know, possessed with an absolute confidence that God is on their side and that victory for them is inevitable.
sentences.zh: 那些士气曾处于谷底的士兵现在似乎，你知道的，充满了绝对的自信，坚信上帝站在他们这一边，胜利对他们来说是不可避免的。

sentences.en: And they attribute this miracle to one person, to Joan the maid.
sentences.zh: 他们将这个奇迹归功于一个人，即圣女贞德。

sentences.en: And this is the news, for instance, that brought to Christine de Pazin, the great poet in the Abbey in seclusion.
sentences.zh: 这也是传给隐居在修道院的伟大诗人克里斯蒂娜·德·皮藏的消息。

sentences.en: In silence, she's been so despondent.
sentences.zh: 在沉默中，她曾如此沮丧。

sentences.en: It's what inspires her to start writing poetry again.
sentences.zh: 正是这一点激发她重新开始写诗。

sentences.en: Christine writes about Joan.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜写下了关于贞德的文字。

sentences.en: The beauty of her life proves that she has been blessed with God's grace.
sentences.zh: 她一生的美好证明了她得到了上帝恩典的赐福。

sentences.en: How clear this was at the siege of Orléans.
sentences.zh: 在奥尔良之围中，这一点是多么清晰明了。

sentences.en: It is my belief that never was a miracle more evident.
sentences.zh: 我相信，再也没有比这更明显的奇迹了。

sentences.en: Crikey.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Well, the story of Joan of Arc is, of course, not yet over because she has promised that she will lead the Dauphin to Rhin for his coronation and drive the English out of France.
sentences.zh: 当然，圣女贞德的故事还没有结束，因为她曾承诺要带领王太子前往兰斯加冕，并将英国人赶出法国。

sentences.en: And we'll discover whether or not they do that.
sentences.zh: 我们将拭目以待他们是否会这样做。

sentences.en: And we will also turn to the question that is now on the Englishman's minds.
sentences.zh: 我们还将转向现在萦绕在英国人心头的问题。

sentences.en: Is Joan really sent from God or is she, as the trial will prove, a witch?
sentences.zh: 贞德真的是由上帝派遣的，还是正如审判将证明的那样，她是一个女巫？

sentences.en: Now, if you're a member of the Rest is History Club, you can hear those episodes right now.
sentences.zh: 如果你是“历史的其余部分”俱乐部的成员，你现在就可以收听这些节目。

sentences.en: You don't need to wait.
sentences.zh: 你不需要等待。

sentences.en: If you'd like to join our club members and enjoy all the amazing benefits that they take great pleasure from every day, then just head to therestishistory.com.
sentences.zh: 如果你想加入我们的俱乐部成员，并享受他们每天津津乐道的所有惊人福利，只需访问 therestishistory.com。

sentences.en: But we will be back to find out what happens next in this extraordinary story and to examine exactly what was going on in Joan of Arc's head.
sentences.zh: 但我们将会回来，了解这个非凡故事的接下来会发生什么，并仔细探究贞德脑海中究竟在想些什么。

sentences.en: So on that bombshell, Tom, merci et au revoir.
sentences.zh: 带着这个爆炸性的消息，汤姆，谢谢你，再见。

sentences.en: Au revoir.
sentences.zh: 再见。
